translations.text: The vision which Isaiah son of Amoz saw, which he saw concerning Judea and Jerusalem, in the reign of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, who reigned in Judea.
Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord was speaking: I have begotten sons and raised them, and they have despised me.
The ox knew its owner, and the donkey the manger of its lord, but Israel did not know me, and my people did not understand me.
Woe to the sinful nation: a people that is full of sin, an evil brood, sons of lawlessness. They have forsaken the Lord and angered the Holy One of Israel.
Why are you still being struck, and adding more lawlessness? The whole head is given over to pain, and the whole body to grief.
From the feet to the head there is no soundness in it: no wound, no bruise, no swollen sore [is tended]. There is no salve to apply, no oil, no bandage.
Your land is desolate, your cities are burned with fire. Strangers devour your dwelling place before your eyes, and it is laid waste and overthrown by a people of foreigners.
And the daughter of Zion has been left like a booth in a vineyard, like a watchman's hut in a melon field, and like a besieged city.
And if the Lord of Hosts had not left us offspring, we would have become like the people of Sodom, and been made like the people of Gomorrah.
Hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom; give heed to the law of God, you people of Gomorrah.
What is the multitude of your sacrifices to me? says the Lord. For I am full of whole burnt offerings of rams and of the fat of lambs, and I do not want the blood of bulls and of goats.
Nor even if you come to appear before me: who required this from your hands, that you should even enter my court?
Do not go on with it any longer. If you bring me an offering of fine flour, it is futile, and incense is an abomination to me.
Your new moons and sabbaths and the great day have not pleased me. My soul hates your fasting, your rest days and your feasts, for you have become a surfeit to me. I will no longer forgive your sins.
When you stretch out your hands to me, I will turn my face away from you; and if you multiply your prayers, I will not hear you, for your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean, remove the wickedness from your souls before my eyes; cease from your evil deeds.
Learn to do good, seek out justice, rescue the oppressed, give judgment for the orphan and vindicate the widow.
And come, let us reason together, says the Lord. Even if your sins are like dye, I will make them white as snow; and though they are like purple, I will make them white as wool.
And if you are willing and listen to me, you will eat the good things of the land.
If you are not willing and do not listen to me, the sword will devour you, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken this.
How has Zion, the faithful city, become a harlot! It was full of justice, and righteousness rested in it. But now it is filled with murder.
Your silver is dross; your wine-sellers mix the wine with water.
Your rulers are disobedient and partners of thieves. They love bribes and chase after payback. They do not give judgment for the orphan, and they do not attend to the cause of widows.
Therefore thus says the Lord God of Sabaoth, the Mighty One of Israel: My anger shall not cease against my adversaries, and I will execute judgment on my enemies.
And I will lay my hand upon you, and I will refine you to purity by fire; but the disobedient I will destroy, and I will take away all lawlessness from you, and I will humble all the proud.
And I will set up your judges as at first, and your counsellors as in the beginning. And after this you shall be called the city of righteousness, the faithful mother-city, Zion.
For her captives shall be saved by judgment and by mercy.
And the lawless and the sinners shall be crushed together, and those who have forsaken the Lord shall be destroyed,
for they shall be ashamed of their idols, which they desired, and they were ashamed of their carved images, which they made. And they shall be ashamed of their gardens, which their heart craved.
For they were like terebinths that have shed their leaves, and like a garden that has no water.
And their strength shall be like tow of flax, and their works like sparks of fire; and the lawless and the sinners shall be burned together, and there shall be no one to quench them.
The word that came to Isaiah the son of Amoz concerning Judea and Jerusalem.
For in the last days the mountain of the Lord shall be made manifest, and the house of God on the top of the mountains; and it shall be exalted above all the hills.

And all the nations shall come there, and many peoples shall come and say: Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will tell us his way, and we will walk in it. For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

And he shall judge among the peoples and shall rebuke many people; and they shall beat their swords into ploughshares and their spears into sickles, and nation shall not lift up sword against nation, and they shall no longer learn war any more.
And now, you house of Jacob, come and let us walk in the light of the Lord,

for he has forsaken his people, the house of Jacob, because their land was filled, as from the beginning, with divination like that of the foreigners, and many children of foreigners were born to them.
For their land was filled with silver and gold, and there is no number to their treasures.
And their land was filled with horses, and there is no number to their chariots. And their land was filled with abominations, the works of their hands. And they worshipped what was made with fingers.
And man has bowed down, and the male has been humbled; and do not forgive them any more.
And now enter into the rocks and hide yourselves in the earth from before the fear of the Lord and from the glory of his might, when he rises to shatter the earth.
For the eyes of the Lord are lofty, but man is lowly; and the loftiness of man has been brought low, and God alone has been exalted on that day.
For the day of the Lord of Sabaoth shall come upon all the insolent and the proud, and upon everything high and lofty,
and upon every cedar of Lebanon,
and upon every high mountain, and upon every high hill,
and upon every high wall, and upon every high tower,
and upon every ship of the sea, and upon every sight of the beauty of ships.
Every man shall be humbled, and the Lord alone shall be exalted on that day,
And they shall hide away all the things made by hands,
and they shall carry them into the caves and the clefts of the rocks and the holes of the earth, from before the fear of the Lord and from the glory of his might.
For in that day a man shall cast away his handmade things of silver and of gold, which they made for themselves to worship, to the vain things and to the bats,
to go into the holes of the solid rock and into the clefts of the rocks, from before the fear of the Lord and from the glory of his might, when he rises up to shake the earth.
Behold, the Sovereign, the Lord of Sabaoth, takes away from Judea and from Jerusalem the strong man and the capable woman, the strength of bread and the strength of water,
the hero and the mighty one and the man of war, and the judge and the prophet, and the one who gives ordinances, and the elder,
and the captain of fifty, and the wonderful counsellor, and the wise man and the master builder, and the understanding listener.
And I will set youths over them as rulers, and mockers shall rule over them.
And the people shall fall, man against man, and each man against his neighbour. The youth shall rise against the elder, and the dishonoured against the honourable.
For a man shall take hold of his brother, or of one of his father's household, and say to him: “You have a garment; be a leader for us, and let our food be under your charge.”
And in that day he shall answer him and say: “I will not be a leader, for there is neither bread nor garment in my house. I will not be the leader of this people.”
For Jerusalem is forsaken and Judea has fallen, and their tongues, with lawlessness, are disobedient toward the Lord. Therefore their glory has now been brought low,

and the shame of their face has risen up against them, and they have proclaimed and displayed their sin like that of the Sodomites. Woe to their soul, for they have devised an evil plan against themselves,
and they said: “Let us bind the righteous one, for he is troublesome to us.” Now therefore they shall eat the fruit of their deeds.
Woe to the lawless one: evil shall befall him according to the works of his hands.

O my people, your tax collectors glean you bare, and those who exact payment from you are the very ones who rule over you. O my people, those who call you blessed lead you astray and unsettle the path of your feet.
Now the Lord shall stand up for judgement, and he shall bring his people forward for judgement,
and the Lord himself shall come into judgement with the elders of the people and with its rulers: “Why have you burned my vineyard? And the plunder of the poor is found in your houses.
Why do you wrong my people and put the face of the poor to shame?”

Therefore the Lord says: Because the daughters of Zion have become haughty, and walked with outstretched necks and winking eyes, and as they walked they trailed their garments along, and they skipped about with their feet,
God shall humble the noble daughters of Zion, and the Lord shall expose their form
in that day. And God shall take away the glory of their apparel, and their ornaments, and their braided headbands [?], and their fringes [?], and their crescents [?],
and their ointment boxes [?], and the ornament of their face,
and the set of jewellery that made up their glory, and the armlets and the bracelets, and the braided locks, and the rings, and their [?], and the earrings,
and the purple garments and the [?], and the fine things of Laconia,
[?] stone,
and of fine linen, and of blue, and of purple, and the zelezi [?] woven together with gold and with blue, and the bialon [?] veils of [?].

And instead of sweet-smelling perfume there will be dust; instead of a sash you will gird yourself with a rope; instead of an ornament for the head, baldness will come upon you because of your deeds; and instead of a garment of mixed [?] scarlet you will put on sackcloth. This will be your adornment.
And your finest son, the one you love, will fall by the sword, and your mighty men will perish by the sword and be brought low.
And the storehouses of your ornaments will mourn,

and you will be left alone and brought low to the ground. And seven women will take hold of one man and say to him: "We will eat our own bread and wear our own clothes; only let your name be called upon us, and take away our disgrace."
On that day God will make the remnant of Israel shine on the earth with glory of counsel, to exalt and glorify it.
And the remnant of Israel will be in Zion, and the remnant in Jerusalem will be called holy: those who are written down for life in Jerusalem.
For the Lord will wash away the filth of the sons and daughters of Zion, and will cleanse the blood of Jerusalem from its midst by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.

And he will come, and it will be so: over every place on Mount Zion and every place around it, a cloud will give shade by day, and by night there will be something like smoke of fire and a brightness of light; and it will give shade with all glory.
And it will be a shade to cover from the heat, and a shelter from heat and rain.
I will sing to my beloved a song of my beloved about my vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on an honoured, fertile place.

And I put a hedge around it, and fenced it with stakes, and planted a choice vine, and built a tower in it, and dug a winepress in the middle of it; and I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
And now, man of Judah, and you who live in Jerusalem, judge between me and my vineyard:
What more should I have done for my vineyard that I did not do for it? For I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
Now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will tear down its hedge, and it will be plundered; I will break down its wall, and it will be trampled;
and I will abandon my vineyard, and it will be neither pruned nor dug, and thorns will spring up in it as in a wasteland. And I will command the clouds not to rain any rain upon it.

For the vineyard of the Lord of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the man of Judah is his beloved new planting. I waited for him to do justice, but he did lawlessness; not righteousness, but an outcry.
Woe to those who join house to house and add field to field, so that they may seize something of their neighbour's! Will you then dwell alone on the earth?

For this has been heard in the ears of the Lord of Hosts: even if there are many houses, they will be turned into desolation; and even if they are very great and beautiful, there will be found no one to live in them.
Where ten yoke of oxen work, it will yield one jar of wine; and whoever sows three sowing-measures will yield three measures.
Woe to those who rise at dawn and pursue drunkenness, and stay at it until evening, and make the night [?]; for the wine will inflame them.
For they drink wine with harps and lyres and drums and pipes, but they do not look at the works of the Lord, and they do not consider the works of his hands.
So now my people have been taken captive, because they did not know the Lord, and their dead have multiplied through hunger and thirst for water.
And Hell has stretched its body wide. It has opened its mouth so that it will not lack anything, and its glorious ones, its great ones, its rich and its defiled ones go down into it.
Man will be brought low, the male will be dishonored, and the proud eyes will be brought low.
But the Lord Sabaoth will be exalted in judgment, and the holy God will be glorified in righteousness.
And those who were plundered will graze like bulls, and lambs will graze in the desert of the forsaken.
Woe to those who drag their sin along as if with a long rope, and their lawlessness as if with the strap of a heifer's yoke,
who say, "Let God hurry up and do what he will do, so that we may see it; and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel come, so that we may know it."
Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who make light into darkness and darkness into light, and who make bitter sweet and sweet bitter.
Woe to those who count themselves wise and seem prudent in their own eyes.
Woe to those mighty ones of yours who drink wine, and to those powerful ones of yours who mix mead,
and who declare the false one righteous for a bribe and take away justice from the righteous.

Therefore, as a coal of fire bursts into flame on a reed and the reed burns along with it in the kindled flame, so their root will be like earth, and their flower will rise up like dust. For they did not want to keep the law of the Lord Sabaoth, but they provoked the words of the Holy One.

And the Lord Sabaoth was angry, in wrath, with his people. He laid his hand on them and struck them down. He was angry at the mountains, and their corpses became like dung in the middle of the road. Yet for all this his wrath has not turned back, but his hand is still raised high.
So now he will raise a signal to the distant nations and bring them from the ends of the earth, and look, they are coming fast and soon.
They will not be hungry or grow weary, they will not get drowsy or fall asleep, the belts around their waists will not be loosened, and the straps of their sandals will not break.
Their arrows are swift and their bows are strung. The hooves of their horses are like solid rock, and the wheels of their chariots are like a whirlwind.
They will come on like lions and rise up like lions' cubs. It will seize its prey and roar like a wild beast and carry it off, and there will be no one to rescue them.
On that day their roaring will be like the roar of a raging sea. They will look up to heaven and down to the earth, and behold, there will be harsh darkness, darkness in their bewilderment.
In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on high and exalted thrones, and the temple was full of the glory of the Lord.
And seraphim stood around him. One had six wings, and the other had six. With two they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
They called out to one another and said, "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord Sabaoth; the heavens and the earth are full of his glory."
And the lintel of the gates was lifted up by the voice with which they were crying out. And the temple was filled with incense,

and I said: Woe is me, wretched one, for I am pierced with grief, for I am a man and I have unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people who have unclean lips. And I have seen the King, the Lord of Sabaoth, with my own eyes.
And one of the seraphim was sent to me, and in his hand he had a live coal, which he had taken with tongs from the altar,
and he touched it to my mouth and said: Behold, I have touched this to your lips, and your iniquities have been wiped away and your sins have been cleansed.
And I heard the voice of the Lord, and he said: Whom shall I send, or who will go to that people? And I said: Behold, here I am; send me.
And he said: Go and say to that people: Hearing you will hear, and you will not understand; and seeing you will see, and you will not perceive,

for the heart of this people has grown fat, and they have heard heavily with their ears, and they have closed their eyes, lest they see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart, and turn back, and I heal them.
And I said: How long, O Lord? And he said: Until the cities are laid waste so as to be uninhabited, and the houses, so that there are no people in them, and the land is left desolate.
And after this God will remove people far away, and those who have been left on the earth will be multiplied,
and there will still be a tenth on it, and again they will be plundered, like a terebinth, and like an acorn when it falls out of its husk.

And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz son of Jotham son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin king of Aram came up, and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, to Jerusalem to make war against it. And they could not besiege it.
And they told the house of David, saying: Aram has conspired together with Ephraim. And his soul was shaken, and the soul of his people, as a tree in the forest is shaken by the wind.
And the Lord said to Isaiah: Go out to meet Ahaz king of Judah, you and the remnant, Jashub your son, at the pool on the upper side of the road of the fuller's field,

and say to him: Take care to keep silent, and do not be afraid, and do not let your heart grow faint because of these two smoking firebrands of wood; for when the wrath of my anger has passed, I will bring healing again.
And the son of Remaliah and the son of Aram have devised an evil plan against you, and they said:
Let us go up to Judea and talk with them, and turn them over to our side, and let us make the son of Tabeel king over it.
Thus says the Lord of Sabaoth: That plan shall not stand, nor shall it come to pass.
But the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and after sixty-five years more the kingdom shall be taken away from Ephraim.
And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. And if you do not believe, neither will you understand.
The Lord spoke again to Ahaz and said:
Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God, in the depth or in the height.
And Ahaz said: I will not ask, nor will I put the Lord to the test.
And Isaiah said: Hear now, O house of David: Is it a small thing for you to cause people trouble? How then will you cause trouble for the Lord?
Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and she shall call his name Emmanuel.
He shall eat butter and honey until he knows, or until he chooses: he shall reject the evil and choose the good.
For before the child knows good or evil, he shall reject the evil and choose the good. And the land which you fear shall be forsaken before those two kings.
But he shall bring upon you, and upon your people, and upon the house of your father, days that have not yet come, from the day when Ephraim took away from Judah the king of the Assyrians.
And it shall be on that day that the Lord shall send forth the fly, which rules part of the river of Egypt, and the bee which is in the land of Assyria.
And they shall come and settle in all the valleys of the lands, and in the holes of the rocks, and in the caves, and in all the clefts, and on all the trees.
On that day the Lord shall shave with the drunken razor beyond the river: the head of the king of the Assyrians and the hair of the feet, and he shall shave the beard.
And it shall be on that day that a man shall rear a heifer of the cattle and two sheep.
And it shall be that, because of the abundance of milk, all who are left in the land shall eat butter.
And it shall be on that day that every place where there were a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels shall become waste and thorns.
With arrow and bow they shall go in there, for all the land shall be waste and thorns.
And every mountain shall be ploughed with the plough, and no fear shall come there; for out of the waste and thorns it shall become a pasture for sheep and a place trampled by cattle.
And the Lord said to me: Take for yourself a new, large roll of paper, and write on it with a man's pen, so that the spoil may be carried off quickly, for it is at hand.
And make faithful men witnesses for me: Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Barachiah.
And I went in to the prophetess, the maiden, and she conceived and bore a son. And the Lord said to me: Call his name 'Plunder quickly, carry off swiftly.'
For before the child knows how to call the name of father or mother, he shall grow strong and carry off the power of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria before the kings of Assyria.
And the Lord spoke to me again, and said:
Because this people does not want the water of Siloam that flows gently, but you want Rezin and the son of [?Remaliah] as king over you,

therefore, behold, the Lord shall bring up upon you the water of the river, strong and abundant: the king of Assyria and all his glory. And he shall come up over all your valleys and shall walk over all your walls.
And he shall take away from Judea any man who could lift up his head, or who could accomplish anything [?]; and his camp shall be such that it fills the breadth of your land. God is with us.
Know, you nations, and be defeated; listen, to the end of the earth. You who have grown strong, be defeated. If you grow strong again, you shall be defeated again.
And whatever counsel you devise, the Lord shall bring it to nothing; and the word that you speak shall not stand with you, for God is with us.
Thus says the Lord with a strong hand, concerning those who are disobedient, and concerning walking in the way of this people; and they say:
Do not call anything hard, for everything that this people says is hard. Do not fear what they fear, and do not be terrified of them.
Make the Lord himself holy, and he shall be your fear.

And if you trust in him, he shall be a sanctuary for you. You shall not run into him as a stone of stumbling, nor as a rock of offence. But the house of Jacob dwells in Jerusalem in a snare and in offence.
Therefore many shall become weak. They shall fall and be crushed, and they shall come near and be caught, men who are cautious.
Then those who are sealed will be revealed, so that they do not learn the law.
And he will say: "I will wait for God, who has turned his face away from the house of Jacob, and I will trust in him."
Behold, I and the children whom God has given me. They shall be signs and portents in the house of Israel from the Lord of Hosts (Sabaoth), who dwells on Mount Zion.

And if they say to you, "Seek out the ventriloquists and those who call up spirits from the earth, who speak from the belly", is not a people bound to its God? For they consult the dead on behalf of the living.
For the law was given as a help, so that they would not speak like this word, about which there is no giving of bribes.

And a severe famine shall come upon you. When you are hungry, you will be distressed, and you will speak evil of the ruler and of the worldly ones [?]. And they will lift their eyes up to heaven above

and down to the earth below. And behold, there is a dire lack of bread, and darkness, affliction and distress, and gloom so thick that one cannot see. Yet whoever is in distress shall not be lost until the time.
Do this first, quickly, O land of Zebulun, land of Naphtali, and the others who live by the seacoast, and beyond the Jordan, the region of Galilee of the Gentiles.
The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. You who dwelt in the land of the shadow of death, a light has shone upon you.
The greater part of the people, whom you have brought down in your joy, shall rejoice before you, like those who rejoice at the threshing floor and like those who divide the spoil.
For the yoke that was laid upon them has been taken away, and the rod that was on their neck. For he has done away with the rod of the rebellious, as on the day of Midian.
For they shall repay every garment gathered by deceit and every ornament in exchange, and they shall wish that they had been burned with fire.

For a child has been born to us, a son, and has been given to us, whose dominion was upon his shoulders. And his name shall be called Angel of Great Counsel, Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Sovereign, Prince of Peace, Father of the age to come. For I will bring peace upon the rulers, peace and life to him.

Great is his dominion, and there is no limit to his peace. He shall sit upon the throne of David, his kingdom shall prosper for him, and he shall strengthen it with righteousness and justice from now on and forever. The zeal of the Lord of Hosts (Sabaoth) has done all this.
The Lord sent death upon Jacob, and it came upon Israel,
and all the people of Ephraim shall know it, and those who dwell in Samaria, who speak with insolence and a haughty heart:
"The bricks have fallen, but come, let us hew out stones and cut down sycamores and firs, and build a tower for ourselves."
And God shall strike down those who have risen up on the mountain, on Zion and Jerusalem, and shall destroy the enemies of Judah.
The Assyrians from the east and the Greeks from the west, who devour my people with every mouth. For all this his anger has not turned away, but his hand is still raised.
And the people did not turn back until they were struck, and they did not seek the Lord.
And the Lord cut off from Israel head and tail, great and small, in one day: the old man and those who show respect to persons. This is the head.
And the prophet who teaches lawlessness, this is the tail.
And those who called this people blessed were going astray, and they led them astray so that they might swallow them up.

Therefore God will not rejoice over their young men, and he has not had mercy on their orphans, for all are lawless and wicked. Every mouth speaks falsehood. For all this his anger has not turned away, but his hand is still raised.
And lawlessness will burn like fire, and like dry stubble it will be consumed by fire. It will blaze up in the thickets of the forests and will devour everything around the hills together.
Through the anger of the Lord's wrath the whole earth is burned up together. And the people will be like those burned by fire; a man will not have mercy on his brother,
but will turn to the right, for he will be hungry, and he will devour from those on the left, and a man will not be satisfied by eating the flesh of his own arm.
For Ephraim will eat Manasseh's flesh, and Manasseh Ephraim's, for together they will besiege Judah.
For all this his anger has not turned away, but his hand is still raised.
Woe to those who write wickedness, for they write, and what they write is wickedness,
who pervert the judgment of the fallen and seize away the justice due to the poor of my people, so that widows might be plunder for them and orphans prey to be carried off.

And what will they do on that day of visitation? For your affliction will come from afar, and to whom will you flee to find help? And where will you leave your glory, so that you do not fall to those who lead you away captive? And they will fall beneath the slain.
And for all this his anger has not turned away, but his hand is still raised.
Woe to the Assyrians, the rod of my anger, and wrath is in their hands.
I will send my wrath against a lawless nation, and against my people I will command plunder and spoil, and the trampling of cities, and that they be made like the dust of the roads.
But he did not intend it so in his heart, nor did he plan it so in his soul; rather, he turned aside in his mind to destroy nations, and not a few.
And if they say to him, "Are you not the only ruler?"
he will say, "Have I not taken the land above Babylon, and Calneh, where the tower was built? And I took Arabia, and Damascus, and Samaria.
As I took these, so I will take every land." Wail, you carved images in Jerusalem and in Samaria,
and you things made by hands.

When the Lord has finished doing all this on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, he will bring punishment upon that great mind, upon the ruler of the Assyrians, and upon the loftiness of the glory of his eyes.
For he said, "By my strength I will do it, and by the wisdom of my understanding I will seize the boundaries of the nations and carry off their strength."

And I have shaken inhabited cities, and I have seized the whole world with my hand like nestlings, and I have gathered them up like abandoned eggs, and there is no one who can escape me or speak a word against me.

Shall the axe glorify itself without the one who cuts with it, or shall the saw exalt itself without the one who draws it? It is the same as if someone were to lift up a rod or a [?] (stick?), and it is not so.
Rather, the Lord Sabaoth will send dishonor upon your honor, and a kindled fire will blaze up upon your glory.
And the light of Israel will be like a kindled flame, and he will sanctify it and burn it, and it will devour the forest like hay.
On that day the mountains and hills and thickets will dry up, and it will devour from soul to flesh, and the one who flees will be like someone fleeing from a kindled flame.
And those of them who remain will be so few in number that a small child could write them down.
On that day the remnant of Israel will no longer increase, and the saved of Jacob will no longer trust in those who harmed them. Instead they will trust in God, the Holy One of Israel, in truth,
and the remnant of Jacob will turn back to the Mighty One.
And even if your people, Israel, are like the sand of the sea, only their remnant will be saved.
For the Lord will carry out a word upon the whole world, a word that brings to completion and is cut short in righteousness, for it is a word cut short.

Therefore the Lord Sabaoth says this: My people who live in Zion, do not be afraid of the Assyrians, for they will strike you with a rod. For I will bring a blow upon you, so that you may see the way of Egypt.
Yet a little while, and my wrath against you will cease, but my anger will be upon their counsel.
And God will raise up torment against them, like the blow against Midian in the place of distress, and his anger will be on the way by the sea toward Egypt.
And on that day his yoke will be taken from your neck, and the fear of him will be taken from you, and his yoke will be destroyed from your shoulders.
For he will come to the city of Angai,
and pass through Maggedo, and at Michmash he will lay down his baggage.
And he will cross the ravine and reach Gibeon, and turn back. Fear will seize Ramah, the city of Saul.
And the daughter of Gallim will flee. Laish will hear, Anathoth will hear,
Madmenah is dismayed, and the inhabitants of Gebim.

Today they prayed to stop on the way. With their hands they pleaded to the mountain of the daughter of Zion and the hills that were in Jerusalem and Judah. Behold, the Lord Sabaoth will throw the mighty into terror with his power.
And the lofty will be crushed in disgrace, and the proud will be brought low, and the lofty will fall by the sword, and Lebanon will fall with its height.
And a rod will come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower will spring up from his root,
and the Spirit of God will rest upon him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and godliness.
And the spirit of the fear of God will fill him. He will not judge according to reputation, nor will he reprove according to what is said,

but he will judge with righteous judgment, and he will reprove the great of the earth. He will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he will destroy the ungodly.
And his loins shall be girded with righteousness, and his sides wrapped with truth.
Then the wolf shall graze with the lambs, and the leopard shall rest with the kids, and the calf and the lion and the young bull shall graze together; and a [?] little child shall gather them.
The ox and the bear shall graze together, and their young shall live together, mixed with one another; and the lion shall eat straw like the ox.
And a little child shall put his hand on the hole of the asp and on the nest of the asps' young, and they shall do him no harm.
And they shall not be able to destroy anyone on my holy mountain, for the whole earth has been filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as abundant water covers the sea.
And in that day there shall be the root of Jesse, he who rises up to rule over the Gentiles; in him the Gentiles shall hope, and his resting place shall be in honour.

And in that day the Lord shall once more show his hand, to be zealous for and to seek out the remaining remnant of the people, those left by the Assyrians, and from Egypt and Babylon, and from Ethiopia, and from the Elamites, and from the rising of the sun, and from Arabia.
And he shall raise a sign for the Gentiles, and he shall gather the lost of Israel, and he shall gather the scattered of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
And the jealousy of Ephraim shall be taken away, and the enemies of Judah shall perish. Ephraim shall no longer be jealous of Judah, and Judah shall no longer be jealous of Ephraim,
and they shall fly in the ships of foreigners; together they shall plunder the sea of the east and Idumea. They shall first lay hands on Moab, and the sons of Edom shall be the first to submit.
And the Lord shall lay waste the sea of Egypt, and lay his hand on the river with a fierce wind, and divide it into seven ravines, so that it can be crossed in sandals.
And it shall be a way out for the remnant of my people in Egypt, and it shall be for Israel as on the day when it came out of the land of Egypt.
And you shall say in that day: May the Lord bless you, for you were angry with me; and you turned away your anger and had mercy on me.
Behold, my God, my Saviour, the Lord; I will trust in him and be saved by him, and I will not be afraid, for he is my glory and my praise, and he has become my Saviour.
And you shall draw water with joy from the springs of salvation.
And you shall say in that day: Sing to the Lord; cry out in his name. Proclaim his glory among the Gentiles. Remember that his name has been exalted.
Sing to the name of the Lord, for he is exalted; proclaim this in all the earth.
Rejoice and be glad, you who dwell in Zion, for the Holy One of Israel has been exalted in her midst.
The vision concerning Babylon, which Isaiah son of Amoz saw.
Raise a sign on the mountains of the plain; lift up your voice to the mountains. Give comfort with the hand. Open the gates, you rulers.
I give the command; they are sanctified, and I bring them. Mighty men are coming to satisfy my anger, rejoicing together and insulting.
The sound of many nations on the mountain, like the sound of many nations; the sound of the kings of the Gentiles gathered together.
The Lord of Hosts commands an armed, warlike nation to come from far away, from the edge of the foundation of heaven: the Lord and his armed warriors, to destroy the world.
Cry out, for the day of the Lord is near, and destruction shall come from God.
Therefore all hands will grow weak, and every human soul will be afraid,

and the messengers will tremble, and pains will seize them like those of a woman in labour. Evil will come on one neighbour together with another, and they will be dismayed, and their faces will change as if from a flame.
For behold, the day of the Lord is coming, without cure, with wrath and anger, to make the whole world a desolation and to destroy the sinners out of it.
For the stars of heaven and Orion and all the adornment of heaven will not give their light. The rising sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light.
And I will decree evil for the whole world, and for the ungodly their sins. I will destroy the insolence of the lawless, and I will bring low the insolence of the proud.
And those who are left will be more precious than unrefined gold, and a man will be more precious than the carbuncle from Sophir.
For the heavens will be enraged, and the earth will be shaken from its foundations by the wrath of the anger of the Lord of Sabaoth, on the day when his wrath comes.
And the remnant will be like fleeing gazelles and like straying sheep, and there will be no one to gather them. Each man will turn back to his own people, and each man will turn back to his own land.
Whoever is caught will be overcome, and those who have been gathered will fall by the sword.
Their children will be dashed to pieces before them, their wives will be carried off, and their houses will be plundered.
Behold, I will raise up against you the Medes, who have no regard for silver and have no need of gold.
They will break the bows of the young men. They will not have mercy on your children, and their eyes will not spare your offspring.
And Babylon, which the kings of the Chaldeans call glorious, will be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.
It will not be inhabited for all ages, and people from many nations will not enter it. Arabians will not pass through it, and shepherds will not rest in it.
Instead, wild beasts will rest there, and their houses will be filled with howling. Monsters will rest there, and demons will dance there.
Wild asses will live there, and hedgehogs [?] will make nests in its houses. It will come swiftly upon the temples of their delight and will not delay, and its days will not be prolonged.
And the Lord will have mercy on Jacob and will once again choose Israel. They will rest in their land, the borders of the land will be added to them, and they will be joined to the house of Jacob.

The nations will bring them and lead them into their own place. They will possess it and multiply on God's land as male and female servants. Those who took them captive will become captives, and they will rule over those who ruled over them.
On that day the Lord will give you rest from your pain, from wrath, and from the harsh slavery in which you serve them.
You will take up this lament over the king of Babylon and say on that day: "The oppressor has ceased, and the one who drove others on has been silenced."
The Lord has broken the yoke of the sinners and the yoke of the rulers, and has struck down the nations with incurable blows,
striking down the nations in wrath and wounding them, and he did not spare them.
The whole earth has come to rest in hope and cries out with joy.
And the trees of Lebanon rejoiced over you, and the firs of Lebanon said to you: "Since you have fallen asleep, no one has come up to cut us down."
Hell below was embittered at meeting you. When you came, it raised up against you the giants who ruled the earth, who rose from their thrones, all the kings of the nations.
All of them will answer and say to you: "You too have been taken, as we were, and you are counted among us."
Your glory has gone down to hell, and your great gladness. They will spread decay beneath you, and the worm will be your covering.
How the star that rises at dawn has fallen from heaven! The one who sent forth against all the nations has been crushed to the earth.
You said in your mind: "I will go up to heaven, above the stars of heaven, and I will set up my thrones, and I will sit on a high mountain, on the high mountains in the north.
I will go up above the clouds, and I will be like the Most High."
But now you have gone down to hell, to the foundations of the earth.
Those who knew you will marvel at you and say: "This is the man who angered the earth, who stirred up kings,
who made the whole world a desolation and tore down its cities. He did not release the captives to their homes."
All the kings of the nations have fallen asleep in honour, each in his own house.
But you have been cast out on the mountains like a loathsome corpse, with the many dead, with those pierced by the sword who go down to hell. Just as a garment soaked in blood will not be clean,
you have destroyed my land and killed my people. You will not remain forever, wicked seed.
Prepare your children for slaughter because of the sin of your father, so that they may not rise up and take possession of the earth and fill the earth with war.
"And I will rise up against them," says the Lord of Hosts, "and I will destroy his name, his remnant, and his offspring." Thus says the Lord of Hosts:
"I will make Babylon a desolation, so that [?] (perhaps hedgehogs) will live in it, and it will be nothing. And I will make it a pit of clay, for destruction."
Thus says the Lord of Hosts: "As I have spoken, so it will be, and as I have planned, so it will stand:
to destroy the Assyrians from my land and from my mountains, and they will be trampled down. Their yoke will be taken from them, and their [?] (perhaps burden) will be removed from their necks."
This is the plan that the Lord has made for the whole world, and this is the hand raised high over all the nations.
For who can cancel what the holy God has planned? And who can turn back his high hand?
The sixth vision, concerning the Philistines. This word came in the year that King Ahaz died.

Do not rejoice, all you foreigners, because the yoke of your oppressor has been broken. For the offspring of asps will come out of the seed of serpents, and flying serpents will come out of their offspring.
The poor will be [?] (literally "brought to an end") by the Lord, and the fallen will rest in peace. But famine will destroy your offspring, and your remnant will be destroyed.
Cry out, you gates of the city! Wail, you terrified cities, among its appointed ones!
And what will they answer the kings of the nations? That the Lord has founded Zion, and through him the lowly of the people will be saved.
The word concerning Moab. By night the Moabite has perished, for by night the wall of the Moabite will perish.
Grieve for yourselves, for Dibon has perished, where the altar was built. There you will go up weeping to Nebo of the Moabite. Wail! Baldness on every head, and all arms cut.
In her streets gird yourselves with sackcloth, and beat yourselves on her roofs, and in her streets wail, all of you, with weeping,
for Heshbon and Elealeh have cried out; their cry was heard as far as Jahaz. Therefore the loins of the Moabite cry out; his soul will know.

The heart of the Moabite cries out over itself as far as Zoar, for it is a three-year-old heifer. And on the ascent of Luhith they went up to you weeping, on the road of Horonaim; they cried out about ruin and misery and quaking.
The water of Nimrim will be desolate, and it has dried up, and all its grass will fail, for there will be no green grass.
Can this one also be saved? For I will bring the Arabs against its valleys, and they will carry it away.
For cry has followed upon cry at the border of the Moabite, at Eglaim; her wailing reaches as far as the well of Elim.
And the water of Rimmon will be filled with blood, for I will bring the Arabs against Rimmon, and I will take away the offspring of Moab and of Ariel and the remnant of Adamah.
I will send them out like creeping things on the earth. Is Petra also a desolate place, the mountain of the daughter of Zion?
For you will be like the nestlings of a bird that has flown away, gathered up.

So you were, daughter of Moab. But at the Arnon take more counsel; make for them a shelter of mourning always. At midday they flee as if in darkness. They were struck with dismay. Do not let it weigh on you.
The fugitives of Moab will settle with you; they will be a shelter for you before the face of the pursuers, for your helpers have been taken away, and the ruler who trampled the land has perished.
And a throne will be set up in mercy, and one will sit on it in truth, in the dwelling of David, judging and seeking justice and hastening righteousness.
We have heard of the insolence of Moab, and he is very insolent. I have taken away his arrogance. Your divination is not so, nor is it thus.
The Moabite cries out to the Moabite. All will cry out over those who live by the wall of baked clay.

The plains of Heshbon will be put to shame; the vineyards of Sibmah will mourn. The nations will swallow them up; trample her vineyards as far as Jazer. Do not gather together; wander in the desert. Those sent by him have been left behind, for they have crossed over the sea.

Therefore I wept, as with the weeping of Jazer, for the vine of Sibmah. The people of Heshbon and Elealeh cut down your trees, for I will trample your harvest and your grape harvest, and everything will fall.
And joy and gladness will be taken away from the vineyards. In your vineyards they will not rejoice, and they will not tread out wine in the winepresses, for it has ceased.
Therefore my belly will moan over Moab like a harp, and my inward parts like a wall that you have renewed.
And it will be as though you were put to shame, for Moab has worn himself out at his altars. He will go in to pray to the things made by his hands, and they will not be able to save him.
This is the word that the Lord spoke concerning Moab when he spoke:

And now the Lord spoke and said: Within three years, like the years of a hired laborer, the glory of Moab shall be brought to dishonor, along with all its great wealth. It shall be left with few people, and it shall be without honor.
The word concerning Damascus. Behold, Damascus shall be taken away from among the cities, and it shall become a ruin,
abandoned forever, a fold for flocks and a resting place, and no one shall pass through it.
Ephraim shall no longer have a strong place to take refuge in. There shall be no kingdom in Damascus, and no remnant of the Syrians, for you are no better than the children of Israel and their glory.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: On that day the glory of Jacob shall fail, and the abundance of his glory shall be shaken.
It shall be like someone gathering the standing harvest with his arm and crushing the ears of grain. It shall be like someone gathering ears of grain in a firm valley.
Stubble shall be left in it, or it shall be like the berries of an olive tree: two or three at the very top, and four or five left on its high branches. Thus says the Lord God of Israel.
On that day a person shall trust in his Maker, and his eyes shall look to the Holy One of Israel.
They shall no longer trust in their altars, or in the works of their hands that their fingers made. They shall no longer look to the trees or to their abominations.
On that day your cities shall be abandoned, as the Amorites and the Hivites abandoned them before the children of Israel, and they shall be desolate,
because you have forsaken God your Savior and have not remembered the Lord your helper. Therefore you shall plant an unfaithful plant.

On the day you plant it, you shall go astray. If you sow at dawn, it shall blossom for the harvest, and on the day you reap it, you shall divide it up, as a man's father divides his property among his sons.
Woe to the multitude of many nations! You shall be shaken like a raging sea, and the backs of many nations shall roar like the sea.

Many peoples are like many waters, like much water rushing with violence. They treated them with contempt and drove them far away, like the dust of chaff from the winnowers before the wind, and like dust from cartwheels that the breeze whirls about.
At evening there shall be mourning; before morning it shall be gone.
This is the portion of those who plundered you, and the inheritance of those who took possession of you.
Woe to the land of the wings of ships, beyond the river of Ethiopia,

which sends hostages across the sea and letters by messengers over the waters. For swift messengers go to distant nations and to a foreign and evil people. Woe to the nation beyond, hopeless and trampled down! Now the rivers of the land have been cut [?] for all.
Their country shall be settled like an inhabited country. It shall be raised up from the mountain like a signal, and it shall be heard like the sound of a trumpet.
For thus the Lord said to me: There shall be security in my city, like light in the heat of midday, and it shall be like a cloud of dew in the days of [?]

before the harvest. When the flowering is over and the unripe grape blooms within the flower and brings forth unripe grapes, he shall cut off the small clusters with pruning hooks, and he shall lop off the branches and cut them away.
He shall leave them all together to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth. The birds of the sky shall gather on it, and the beasts of the earth shall come upon it.

At that time gifts will be brought to the Lord of Hosts from an afflicted and grieving people, and from a people great from now on and for all ages to come, a people who trust in him and who have been trampled down. It is in the place of the river of their land, the place where the name of the Lord of Hosts is invoked: Mount Zion.

The vision concerning Egypt. See, the Lord of Hosts sits on light clouds and is coming to Egypt. The idols that hands have made in Egypt will shake before him, and their hearts will grow weak within them.
Egyptians will rise up against Egyptians. A man will fight against his brother, and a man against his neighbour; city will rise against city, and law against law.

The spirit of the Egyptians will be shaken within them. I will bring their plans to nothing. They will go to their gods and their idols for answers, and to those who call up spirits from the earth and those who speak from the belly.
I will hand Egypt over to men, to harsh masters, and harsh kings will rule over them.
This is what the Sovereign Lord of Hosts says.

The Egyptians will drink water from the seashore, but the river will fail and dry up. The rivers will fail, and so will the branches of the river. The pools of water will dry up, and every marsh of reeds and rushes,
and the meadow along the riverbank, everything around the river, and every sown field by the river will dry up under the scorching wind.
The fishermen will groan. All who cast hooks in that river will groan, and those who spread nets and the fishermen will mourn.
Shame will take hold of those who work the [?] flax, and of those who make fine linen.
Their workers will be in pain. All who work with dry [?] will be distressed, and their hearts will ache.
The princes of Tanis will be driven mad. The king's wise advisers will give foolish advice. How can you say to the king, "We are sons of wise men, sons of kings from ancient times"?
So where are your wise men now? Let them tell you and make known to you what the Lord of Hosts has planned against Egypt.
The princes of Tanis have failed, and the princes of Memphis have grown proud, and they will lead Egypt astray, tribe by tribe.
For the Lord has poured a spirit of error into them, and he has led Egypt astray in everything it does, the way a drunk staggers while he vomits.
Nothing the Egyptians do will have head or tail, beginning or end.
On that day the Egyptians will be like women, full of fear and trembling before the terror of the Lord of Hosts, which he will bring on them.
The land of Judea will terrify the Egyptians. Anyone among them who hears it named will be afraid, because of what the Lord of Hosts, the Almighty, has planned against them.
On that day there will be five cities in Egypt that speak the language of Canaan and swear by the name of the Lord of Hosts. One of them will be called the City of Asedek.
On that day there will be an altar to the Lord in the land of Egypt, and a pillar to the Lord at its border.

It will be a lasting sign for the Lord of Hosts in the land of Egypt. For they will cry out to the Lord because of those who oppress them, and the Lord will send them a man who will save them; he will save them through judgment,
And the Lord will be known to the Egyptians, and on that day the Egyptians will know the Lord, and they will offer sacrifice and offering. And they will make vows to the Lord, and fulfil them to him.
And the Lord will strike the Egyptians with wounds, and he will heal them with healing, and they will turn to the Lord, and he will hear them. And he will heal them.
On that day there will be a road from Egypt to the Assyrians, and the Egyptians will serve the Assyrians.
On that day Israel will be the third with the Assyrians and the Egyptians in that blessed land,
which the Lord of Hosts has blessed, saying: Blessed is my people that is in Egypt and in Assyria, and Israel my inheritance.
In the year that Tartan came to Ashdod, when he was sent by Sargon, king of the Assyrians, he fought against it and took Ashdod.

At that time the Lord spoke to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz and said to him: Go, take that sackcloth off your loins, and remove your sandals from your feet. And Isaiah did so, and walked naked and barefoot.
And the Lord said: As my servant Isaiah walks naked and barefoot, for three years there will be signs and portents against the Egyptians and the Ethiopians.
For in this way the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of the Egyptians and the Ethiopians, young and old, naked and barefoot, and he will expose the shame of Egypt.
And the Egyptians will be utterly weakened because of the Ethiopians, in whom they had put their hope and who had been their glory.

And on that day the inhabitants of this land will say: Look, we had trusted that we could flee to them for help, and they could not save themselves from the king of the Assyrians. How then shall we escape?
The vision of the desert. Like a whirlwind that comes out of the desert, coming from the desert, from a fearful land.

It is fearful: a new vision has been told to me. The one who scorns scorns, and the one who acts lawlessly acts lawlessly. The Elamites are against me, and the envoys of the Persians are coming against me. Now I will groan and comfort myself.
Because of this my loins are filled with weakness, and pangs have seized me like a woman giving birth. I did wrong so as not to hear; I hurried so as not to see.
My heart goes astray, and lawlessness covers me; my soul has come to fear.
Prepare the table, eat and drink. Rise up, you princes, prepare the shields.
For this is what the Lord said to me: Go and post a watchman for yourself, and tell me whatever you see.
And I saw two riders, a rider on a donkey and a rider on a camel. Listen to much news.
And call Uriah to the watchtower. The Lord was saying: I stood at my watchpost all day, and I stood at my camp all night.
And look, a rider of the troops was coming. He answered and said to me: Babylon has fallen, and all her idols and all the works of her hands have been smashed to the ground.
Listen, you who are left and you who are afflicted. Listen to what I have heard from the Lord of Hosts, which the God of Israel has told you.
A word concerning Idumea. Someone calls to me from Seir: Guard the ramparts.
Why do you cry out to the watchman like this through the night? The watchman said: Morning has come, and night. If you seek, then seek, and stay with me in the forest.
A word concerning Arabia. In the forest in the evening they will sleep, on the road of Dedan [?].
Bring water to meet the thirsty, you inhabitants of the land of Teman. Meet the fugitives with bread,

because of the multitude of the fugitives, and because of the multitude of those who have gone astray, and because of the multitude of the sword, and because of the multitude of the fighters, and because of the multitude of the drawn arrows, and because of the multitude of those fallen in battle.
For thus the Lord said to me: Within a year, like the year of a hired laborer, the glory of the sons of Kedar shall fail.
And the remnant of the archers, of the sons of Kedar, the number of the mighty, shall be few, for thus the Lord God of Israel has spoken.
The word concerning the valley of Zion. What has happened to you now, that all of you have gone up to the rooftops in vain?
The city is filled with shouting, a clamorous city. Your wounded are not wounded by the sword, nor are your dead slain in battle.
All your rulers have fled, and those who were captured were harshly bound, and the mighty who were in you fled far away.
Therefore I said: Leave me alone, and I will weep bitterly. Do not press to comfort me over the ruin of the daughter of my people.

For it is a day of trembling, of destruction, of trampling, and of going astray, from the Lord Sabaoth. In the valley of Zion they go astray; from the least to the greatest of them they go astray upon the mountain,
and the Elamites took up shields, men mounted on horses, and a host drawn up in battle array.
And the choicest valleys shall be filled with chariots, and the horsemen shall open your gates,
and they shall lay bare the gates of Judah, and on that day they shall look upon the choice houses of the city.
And they laid bare the hidden places of the houses of the citadel [?] of David, and they saw that they were many, and they turned the water of the old bathing pool into the city.
And they tore down the houses of Jerusalem to fortify the city.
And you made water for yourselves between the two walls, beside the old bathing pool, but you did not lift your eyes to him who first built it, and you did not regard its Maker from afar.
And on that day the Lord Sabaoth called for weeping and lamentation, for shaving the head and girding with sackcloth.
But they made joy and merriment, and slaughtered calves and killed sheep, so that they might eat meat and drink wine. And they said: Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.
And this has been revealed in the ears of the Lord Sabaoth: this sin shall not be forgiven you until you die, says the Lord God of hosts.
Thus says the Lord Sabaoth: Go, enter the chamber of Shebna the treasurer, and say to him:
What do you have here? Or what is yours here, that you have hewn out a tomb for yourself, and made a sepulchre for yourself here on high, and carved a dwelling for yourself in the rock?
Behold, the Lord Sabaoth will drive a man out, and he will crush you and strip you of your adornment and your glorious crown,
and he will cast you into a great and boundless land, and there you will die. And he will bring your fine chariot to dishonor, and the house of your prince to be trampled down.
And you will be removed from your office and from your post.
And on that day I will call my servant Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah.

And I will clothe him with your robe, and I will give him your crown for strength, and I will give your stewardship into his hands. And he shall be like a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to the men of Judah.
And I will give him the glory of David, and he shall rule, and there shall be no one to speak against him. And he shall shut, and there shall be no one to open.
And I appointed him ruler in a sure place, and he shall be a throne of glory for his father's house.
And every glorious one in his father's house shall trust in him, from the small to the great, and they shall hang upon him in that day.
Thus says the Lord Sabaoth: The man who was made firm in a sure place shall be shaken, and shall be taken away and fall. And the glory that was upon him shall be destroyed, for the Lord has spoken.
The word concerning Tyre. Wail, you ships of Carthage, for it has perished, and they no longer come from the land of the Kittim. They have been led away captive.
To whom are they like, the inhabitants of this island, the merchants of the seacoast, who cross the sea over many waters, the race of merchants?
Like the harvest of the threshing floor, it praises the traders [?] of the nations.
Be ashamed, Sidon, said the sea; and the strength of the sea said: I have not been in labour, nor have I given birth; I have not reared young men, nor brought up virgins.
When it is heard in Egypt, anguish shall seize them over Tyre.
Go away to Carthage; wail, you inhabitants of this island.
Was this not your insolence from the beginning, before she was handed over?
Who has devised this against Tyre? Is she lacking, then, or does she have no strength? Her merchants are rulers, and her traders are the nobles of the earth.
The Lord Sabaoth has resolved to bring to nothing the insolence of the glorious, and to bring dishonour on every glorious one on the earth.
Till your land, for ships no longer come from Carthage.
Your hand shall no longer prevail on the sea, which provoked kings to anger; the Lord of hosts has given command concerning Canaan to destroy its strength.
And they shall say: You shall no longer go on insulting and wronging the virgin daughter of Sidon. And even if you go to the Kittim, there will be no rest for you there either,
nor in the land of the Chaldeans; and that too has been laid waste by the Assyrians. There will be no rest for you there either, for its wall has fallen.
Wail, you ships of Carthage, for your stronghold has perished.

And it shall come to pass in that day that Tyre shall be left for seventy years, like the time of one king, like the lifetime of a man; and after seventy years Tyre shall be like the song of a harlot.
Take a lyre and go about, you forgotten harlot city; play well, sing much, so that you may be remembered.
And after seventy years the Lord will visit Tyre, and she shall be restored again to her former state. And she shall be a market for all the kings of the earth,

and her trade and her wages shall be holy to the Lord. They shall not be gathered for them, but for those who dwell before the Lord. All her trade shall be for eating and drinking and for being filled, as a fitting memorial before the Lord.
Behold, the Lord is laying waste the world, and he will make it desolate and lay bare the face of the earth, and he will scatter its inhabitants over it.

And the people shall be like the priest, and the servant like the master, and the maidservant like the mistress; and the seller shall be like the buyer, and the lender like the borrower, and the debtor like the one who gives.
With destruction the earth shall be destroyed, and with plunder the earth shall be plundered, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken this.
The earth mourned, and the world was destroyed. The high ones of the earth mourned.
But the earth committed lawlessness through its inhabitants, for they transgressed the law, and changed the commandments, and annulled the everlasting covenant.
Therefore a curse shall devour the earth, for the inhabitants of the earth have sinned; therefore the inhabitants of the earth shall be poor, and few people shall be left.
The wine shall mourn and the vine shall mourn; all who were glad of heart shall sigh.
The joy of the drums has ceased; the revelry and the wealth of the ungodly have ceased; the sound of the harp has ceased.
They were ashamed and did not drink wine. The strong drink was bitter to those who drank it.
All the cities shall be laid waste; the houses shall be shut, so that no one may enter.
Let them wail for the wine in every place. The joy of the earth has ceased.
The cities shall be left desolate, and the abandoned houses shall perish.
All this shall be on the earth among the nations: as someone gleans an olive tree, so shall they be gleaned, even if the grape harvest has ceased.
These shall cry out aloud, and those who are left on the earth shall rejoice together, for at the glory of the Lord the waters of the sea shall be troubled.
Therefore the glory of the Lord shall be upon the islands, and the name of the Lord, the God of Israel, shall be glorified.
O Lord God of Israel, from the ends of the earth we have heard wonders, the hope of the ungodly, and they shall say: Woe to the scorners, who scorn the law.
Fear and the pit and the snare are upon you who dwell on the earth.

And whoever flees from the fear shall fall into the pit, and whoever comes up out of the pit shall be caught in the snare, for the windows of heaven have been opened, and the foundations of the earth shall be shaken.
It has reeled; the earth shall be utterly shaken, and the earth shall utterly faint.

Like a drunkard and one who is stupefied, it shall be shaken like a watchman's hut in an orchard. The tent of the earth shall fall and shall not be able to rise, for lawlessness has grown strong upon it.
And on that day God shall send his hand against the adornment of heaven and against the kings of the earth.
And he shall gather their assemblies into prison and shut the doors; after many generations they shall be visited.
And the bricks shall be trampled, and the wall shall fall, for the Lord shall reign in Zion, in Jerusalem, and he shall be glorified before the elders.
O Lord my God, I will glorify you and sing praise to your name, for you have done wonderful deeds. Your counsel from the beginning is true. So be it, Lord.
For you have turned cities into dust, and brought strong cities to fall from their foundations. The city of the ungodly shall never be rebuilt.
Therefore the poor people shall bless you, and the cities of oppressed people shall bless you,

For you have become a helper to every lowly city, and a protector of the faint-hearted against want. You will deliver them from wicked men. You are a protector of the thirsty and of the souls of despised men.
For they are like faint-hearted men thirsting in Zion, because of those ungodly men to whom you handed us over,
and the Lord of Hosts will make a feast for all the nations. On the mountain they shall drink gladness, they shall drink wine,
they shall anoint themselves with ointment, and they shall receive it as a gift on this mountain. Give all this to the nations, for this counsel is for all the nations.
Death swallowed them up and prevailed. And again the Lord took away every tear from every face. He took away the reproach of his people from all the earth, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken.
And on that day they shall say, "Behold our God, in whom we trusted, and let us rejoice in our salvation."
God will give rest on this mountain, and Moab shall be trampled down as a threshing floor is trampled with a threshing sledge,
and they shall make his hands idle. Just as he humbled others and destroyed them, so shall he be humbled, and his pride shall be humbled, where he laid his hands.
And he shall bring low the height of the wall of your refuge, and they shall go down to the ground.
On that day they shall sing this song in the land of Judah and say, "Behold a strong city, the city of our salvation. He shall set up a wall and an outer wall."
Open the gates, and let a people enter that has kept righteousness and keeps truth,
and that is a helper of truth and keeps peace. For with hope in you
they trusted in you, O Lord, forever, O great and eternal God,
who humbled and brought down those who dwell on high. You have overthrown strong cities and cast them down to the ground.
And the feet of the lowly shall trample them.
The ways of the godly are straight; the ways of the godly have been made straight and prepared.
For the ways of the Lord are judgment. We trusted in your name and in your remembrance,
which my soul longed for. In the night my soul rose early to seek you, O God, for your commandments are light upon the earth. Learn righteousness, you who dwell on the earth.
For the ungodly has been silenced. He who does not learn righteousness on the earth will not practise truth. Let the ungodly be taken away, so that he does not see the glory of the Lord.
O Lord, your arm is high. They did not know it, but they shall know and be ashamed. Jealousy has seized an untaught people, and now fire has devoured the enemies.
O Lord our God, give us peace, for you have given us everything.
O Lord our God, take us as your own. O Lord, we know no other besides you. We call on your name,
but the dead shall not see life, nor shall physicians raise them up. Therefore you struck them down and destroyed every male among them.
Bring more evils on them, O Lord, bring more evils, bring more evils on the glorious ones of the earth.
O Lord, in affliction we remembered you, for your discipline upon us is slight.
And as a woman in labour, who is near to giving birth, cries out in her pain, so have we become to your beloved one.

Through fear of you, O Lord, we conceived; we were in labour and gave birth. We have brought about the spirit of your salvation on the earth, so that we should not fall, but the inhabitants of the earth shall fall.
The dead shall rise, and those in the tombs shall awaken, and those who sleep on the earth shall rejoice; for the dew that comes from you is healing for them, but the land of the ungodly shall fall.
Go, my people: enter your storeroom, shut your doors before you, and hide yourself for a little while, until the wrath of the Lord passes.
For behold, the Lord sends his wrath from his holy place upon the inhabitants of the earth, and the earth shall reveal its blood and shall not cover the slain.
On that day the Lord will send the holy sword, great and mighty, against the dragon, the crooked serpent, and he will kill the dragon.
On that day there will be a good and desirable vineyard, [?] over it.
I, the strong city, the besieged city: futility watered it. Night will seize it, and by day it will fall.

For there is no wall that has been made firm within it. Who will set me to guard stubble in the field? Because of this war I have despised it. Now therefore, because of this, the Lord has done everything that he commanded.
Those who live in it shall cry out, burned. Let us make peace with him, let us make peace,
you who are coming, children of Jacob. Israel shall sprout and blossom, and the world shall be filled with its fruit.
Shall he then be wounded as he wounded? Or shall he be killed as he killed?
With fighting and reproaches he sent them away. Or is it not you who practised with your fierce spirit to kill them, with a spirit of wrath?

Therefore lawlessness shall be taken away from Jacob, and this is his blessing: when he removes his sin from him, when he makes all the stones of the altars crushed like fine dust, and their idols no longer stand, and their trees are cut down like a distant forest.
And the inhabited flock shall be sent away like an abandoned flock, and it will be a pasture for a long time, and there they will rest.

And after a time there will be no grass on it because of the drought. You women who come from seeing, come, for this is not a people that has understanding. Therefore their maker will not have mercy on them, nor will their creator have mercy on them.
And on that day the Lord will close off the land from the ravine of the river as far as Rhinocorura; and you, gather the sons of Israel one by one.

And on that day they will blow the great trumpet, and those who were lost in Egypt will come, and those who were lost in the land of Assyria, and they will worship the Lord on his holy mountain in Jerusalem.
Woe to the crown of insolence, to the hired labourers of Ephraim, to the fallen flower of glory on the top of the fertile mountain, you who are drunk without wine!

Behold, the anger of the Lord comes mighty and fierce from the Lord. And his wrath is like falling hail where there is no shelter, falling violently, like a mass of water that sweeps away the land. The earth shall have rest.
The crown of insolence, the hirelings of Ephraim, will be trampled under hand and foot.
And the fallen flower of the hope of his glory will be on the summit of the high mountain like an early fig: whoever sees it will want to swallow it even before he takes it into his hands.
On that day the Lord Sabaoth will be the crown of hope, woven of glory, for the remnant of his people.
For they will be left with a spirit of judgment for judgment, and with strength to prevent slaughter.

For these have gone astray through wine; they have erred through strong drink. Priest and prophet were dismayed because of strong drink; they were swallowed up because of wine; they were shaken by the drunkenness of strong drink; they erred. This is the vision. Therefore there is a curse.
It will devour this counsel, for this counsel is for the sake of greed.
To whom have we told this evil, and to whom have we announced the message, you who are weaned from milk, taken from the breasts?
Affliction upon affliction: wait yet [?] a little, hope upon hope, yet [?] a little.
Because of the contempt of their lips, they will speak to this people in another tongue,
and will say to them: "This is rest for the hungry, and this is the command." And they would not listen.
And the word of the Lord will be to them: affliction upon affliction and hope upon hope, yet a little, a little, so that they may go and fall backward, and be crushed, and be in danger, and be taken.
Therefore hear the word of the Lord, you afflicted men, and you rulers of this people who are in Jerusalem.
For you said: "We have made a covenant with hell and an agreement with death. If the rushing storm comes, it will not come upon you; we have made lies our hope, and we will be sheltered by lies."

Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am laying in the foundations of Zion a very precious stone, a chosen cornerstone, precious, a foundation for its foundations; and whoever believes in it will never be put to shame.
And I will make judgment into hope, and my mercy into a balance; and as for those who trusted vainly in lies, [saying,] "For the storm will not pass over us":
will it not take away our covenant of death from us too, and will our hope with hell not stand? If the coming storm passes through, you will be trampled down by it.
Whenever it passes through, it will carry you off; it will pass through in the morning, by day, and at night there will be an evil hope. Learn to listen,
you who are hard pressed: "We cannot fight; we are too weak to be gathered together."

Like a mountain of the ungodly, the Lord will rise up in the valley of Gibeon; he will do his work in wrath, a work of bitterness. But that wrath will act in a strange way, and his bitterness will be strange.
And you, do not rejoice, and let your bonds not be made stronger, for I have heard from the Lord Sabaoth of deeds that are completed and cut short, which he will do upon all the earth.
Give ear and hear my voice; attend and hear my words.
Does a man plow his field all day long in order to sow? Or does he not first prepare it beforehand and work his land?
And when he has leveled its surface, then he sows a little black cumin [?] and cumin, and afterward he sows wheat and barley, millet and spelt, within your borders.
And you will be instructed by the judgment of God, and you will rejoice,
For black cumin is not cleaned out harshly, and no cart-wheel or threshing sledge is rolled over cumin. Instead, the black cumin is beaten out with a rod, and the cumin with a staff,
and it will be eaten with bread. For I will not be angry with you forever, and the voice of my bitterness will not crush you.
These signs came from the Lord of Sabaoth. Take counsel, and raise up empty comfort.
Woe to you, Ariel, the city that David fought against! Gather the harvest year after year, for you will eat with Moab.
I will bring distress on Ariel, and her strength and her wealth will be mine,
and I will surround you as David did. An army will besiege you, and I will build towers around you.

Your words will be brought low to the ground, down to the underworld, and you will be humbled to the ground. You will speak, and your words will sink into the ground. Your voice will be like the voices of those who call out from the earth, and your voice will grow faint, down to the floor of the earth.
The wealth of all the ungodly will be like dust from a wall, and like soil that the wind carries away. It will happen suddenly, in the blink of an eye,
by the Lord Almighty. For he will visit it with thunder and earthquake and a great voice, with a sweeping storm-wind, and with a flame of consuming fire.

The wealth of all the nations will be like a dream in sleep at night: the nations that lined up for battle against Jerusalem, all who rose up against Israel, all who gathered against Jerusalem, and those who oppressed her.

They will be like people who eat and drink in their sleep: when they wake, their vision proves empty. They will be like someone who is thirsty in his sleep and drinks, but when he wakes he is still thirsty, and his soul hoped in vain. So it will be with the wealth of all the nations that lined up for battle against Jerusalem and Mount Zion.
Be amazed and be stunned, and be drunk, but not from wine. Reel, but not from mead, and do not be stirred up by wine,
for the Lord has given us a spirit of grief to drink. He will trouble your eyes, and the eyes of your rulers and of your prophets, who see hidden things.
All these words will be like the words of a sealed book. People give it to a man who knows how to read and say to him, 'Read this,' and he says, 'I cannot read it, for it is sealed.'
Then this book is given into the hand of a man who does not know how to read, and they say to him, 'Read this,' and he says, 'I do not know how to read.'

And the Lord said: 'This people draws near to me with their mouths and honours me with their lips, but their hearts are far removed from me. They serve me in vain, teaching human commandments and doctrines.'
'Therefore, I will go on to remove this people. I will remove them, take away the wisdom of the wise, and hide the understanding of those who understand.'
Woe to those who make their plans deep, and not through the Lord, who make their plans in secret so that their deeds are in darkness, and who say, 'Who sees us, and who will know what we are doing?'

Are you not counted as the potter's clay? Will the thing that was made ever say to its maker, 'You did not make me'? Or will what was created say to its creator, 'You did not make me with understanding'?
Is it not after a short time that Lebanon will be changed to be like Mount Carmel, and Carmel will be counted as a forest?
And on that day the deaf will hear the words of the book, and those who were in darkness and in mist, the eyes of the blind, will see.
And the poor will rejoice in the Lord with joy, and those among men who were given up as lost will be filled with gladness.
And they lay a stumbling block for all who reprove at the gates.
