Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the house of Jacob, which he chose from Abraham: Jacob shall not now be ashamed, nor shall his face now be turned away.
But when their children see my works, for my sake they will hallow my name, and they will hallow the Holy One of Jacob, and they will fear the God of Israel.
And those who went astray in spirit will come to know understanding, and those who murmured will learn to listen, and stammering tongues will learn to speak peace.
Woe to the rebellious children, says the Lord: you have made a plan, but not through me, and a covenant, but not by my Spirit, adding sin upon sin,
you who set out to go down into Egypt, and they did not ask me, for help from Pharaoh and for shelter from the Egyptians.
For the shelter of Pharaoh will become shame for you, and for those who trust in the Egyptians, reproach.
For in Tanis there are leaders, evil messengers.
In vain they will toil for that people, whose help will be of no use to them, but only shame and reproach.

The vision of the four-footed beasts that are in the desert. In affliction and distress, the lion and the lion's whelp come from there, and asps and the offspring of flying asps, who carried their wealth on donkeys and camels to a nation that will be of no use to them.
The Egyptians, vainly and to no purpose, who will be of no use to you. Tell them that this consolation of yours is vain.
Now therefore sit down and write on a tablet and in a book, for this will last for days, and for a time, even forever.
For this is a disobedient people, children of falsehood, who do not wish to hear the law of the Lord,
who say to the prophets, “Do not tell us,” and to those who see visions, “Do not speak to us what is right, but speak to us plainly, and tell us [?].”
“And turn us away from this way, and take these places away from us, and remove from us that word of the Holy One of Israel.”
Therefore thus says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel: because you disobeyed these words and trusted in falsehood, and because you murmured and your heart held fast to this word,
therefore this sin will be to you like a wall falling suddenly, the wall of a strong city under siege, whose fall comes all at once.
And its fall will be like the shattering of an earthen vessel crushed into small pieces, in which no sherd is found with which you could take up fire, or with which you could draw a little water.

Thus says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel: when you turn back and groan, then you will be saved, and you will know where you were when you trusted in those vain things. Your strength came to nothing, and you did not wish to listen.
But you said, “We will flee on horses”; therefore you shall flee. And then you said, “We will ride on swift mounts”; therefore your pursuers will be swift.
And a thousand will flee at the voice of one, and at the voice of five many will flee, until they are left like a web on a mountain, and like a watch-post that stands on a hill.
And then God will wait for you again, to have mercy on you. And so he will be exalted to have mercy on you, because the Lord our God is your judge. Blessed are all who wait patiently for him,
for the holy people will dwell in Zion, and Jerusalem wept bitterly. Have mercy on me with mercy; he will have mercy on you at the sound of your crying out; when he saw you, he heard you.
And the Lord will give you the bread of affliction and the water of distress, and those who lead you astray will no longer come near you, because your eyes will see those who lead you astray.
And your ears will hear the words of those who lead you astray, from behind you [?], who say, “This is the way, and let us walk in it,” whether to the right or to the left.
And you will defile the idols overlaid with silver and overlaid with gold, and you will grind them fine like the water of a woman in her time of separation, and you will scatter them like dung.
Then there will be rain for the seed of your land, and the bread from the produce of your land will be plentiful and rich, and on that day your flocks will graze in a rich and broad place.
Your bulls and oxen that work the land will eat chaff mixed with winnowed barley.
And on every high mountain and on every hill of rest there will be flowing water on that day, when many perish and when the towers fall.

And the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be sevenfold on that day, when the Lord heals the brokenness of his people and relieves the pain of their wound.
Behold, the name of the Lord comes after a long time, his anger burning; the word of his lips is with glory, a word full of wrath, and the wrath of his anger will devour like fire.

And his breath will rush down like water in a ravine, and reach as far as the neck, and it will be divided to terrify the nations, leading them astray in vain. And error will pursue them and carry them off before their faces.

Will you always have joy, and enter my holy place whenever you please, like those who keep a festival, and like those who rejoice to go up with the pipe to the mountain of the Lord, the God of Israel?

And the Lord will make the glory of his voice heard, and the anger of his arm, to show the anger of his wrath with consuming flame, with fierce thunderbolts, and like rain and hail coming down violently together.
For at the voice of the Lord the Assyrians will be weakened by the blow with which he struck them.
And it will be all around him, from where his hope of help came, in which he trusted; with drums, pipes, and harp they will fight against him with [?].

For did you not go astray before that day? Will a kingship be prepared for you too — a kingship of the deep ravine full of wood, fire and wood in great quantity? The anger of the Lord is like a ravine set ablaze with sulfur.

Woe to you who go down to Egypt for help, who trust in horses and chariots, because there are many chariots and a great many horsemen; and they did not trust in the Holy One of Israel, and they did not seek the Lord.
And because he himself is wise, he has brought evil upon them, and his word will not be made void. He will rise up against the houses of wicked men and against their empty hope,
the Egyptian, a man and not God, and the flesh of horses, in which there is no help. But the Lord will lay his hand on them, and those helpers will grow weary, and all of them together will perish.

For thus the Lord said to me: As a lion roars, or a lion's whelp, over the prey it has seized, and cries out over it until the mountains are filled with its voice, and many are startled and tremble at its anger, so the Lord Almighty will come down to encamp on Mount Zion and on its mountains.
Like a bird in flight, so the Lord of hosts will help Jerusalem. He will help it and deliver it, and receive it, and come down, and save it.
Turn back, you sons of Israel, you who devise deep and lawless counsel.
For on that day men will cast away their handmade idols of silver and of gold, which their hands have made,

and Assyria will fall, not by the sword of a man, nor will the sword of a man devour him. He will flee, though not from the face of the sword, and his young men will be weakened, for they will be hemmed in by rock as by a wall. For whoever flees will be caught and will be weakened, and whoever scatters will be given over to defeat.
And their rulers will be given over to defeat in flight, said the Lord, who has fire in Zion and his furnace in Jerusalem. And those who flee will be given over to defeat.
Thus says the Lord: Blessed is the one who has offspring in Zion and a household in Jerusalem. For behold, a righteous king will reign, and rulers will rule with justice.
And there will be a man who hides his words, and he will be sheltered as if from waters rushing violently. And he will appear in Zion like a glorious river flowing into a thirsty land.
And they will no longer trust in men, but they will turn their ears to hear.
And the hearts of the weak will give heed to hear, and stammering tongues will quickly learn the word of peace.
And they will no longer say to the fool, "Rule," and your servants will no longer say, "Be silent."
For the fool will speak folly, and his heart will devise folly, to carry out lawlessness and to speak error against the Lord, to scatter hungry souls and to leave thirsty souls empty.
For the counsel of the wicked devises lawlessness, to ruin the lowly with lying words and to bring to nothing the cause of the lowly in judgment.
But the godly have planned with understanding, and their counsel will stand.
You wives of the rich, rise up and hear my voice; you daughters, listen to my words with hope.
Remember the days of the year in pain, with hope. For the grape harvest is finished; it has ceased and will come no more.
Be astonished and grieve, you women who trust in wealth. Strip yourselves and go naked, and wrap sackcloth around your waists.
And beat your breasts over the pleasant fields and over the fruit of the vine.
In the land of my people thorns and grass will spring up, and joy will be taken away from every house. Rich cities,
and the houses will be left. They will abandon the wealth of the city and the desirable houses. And the villages will be caves forever, and a delight for wild asses, and a pasture for shepherds,
until the Spirit comes upon you from on high. And the wilderness will be like Carmel, and Carmel will be counted as a forest.
And judgment will rest in the wilderness, and righteousness will dwell on Carmel.
And the work of righteousness will be peace, and righteousness will take hold of rest, and they will be confident forever.
And my people will dwell in a city of peace, and they will live there in confidence, and they will rest in wealth.
And if hail comes down, it will not come upon you, and those who live in the forests will be confident, as those on the plain.
Blessed is the one who sows beside every watered place, where the ox and the donkey tread.

Woe to those wretched ones! But no one has made you wretched. The one who treats you with contempt does not treat you with contempt, for those who treat others with contempt will be seized and handed over, and like a moth in a garment, so they will be worn away.
Lord, have mercy on us, for we trust in you. The offspring of the disobedient has become destined for destruction, but our salvation is from you in the time of affliction.
At the sound of the fear of you the peoples were terrified, and before your majesty the nations were scattered.
But now our spoils will be gathered, from the small to the great. As someone gathers locusts, so they will mock you.
Holy is God, who dwells on high. Zion has been filled with judgment and righteousness,
and they will be given over to the law. Our salvation is in treasuries. Wisdom and knowledge and godliness toward the Lord are coming; these are the treasures of righteousness.
Behold, they will fear your fear. Those you were afraid of will be afraid of you. Envoys were sent to ask for peace; they weep bitterly,
for their roads have been laid waste. The fear of the nations has ceased, and the covenant with them has been taken away, and you will not count them as men.
The land mourned; Lebanon was put to shame. Sharon became marshes [?]; Galilee and Carmel were laid bare.
"Now I will arise," says the Lord. "Now I will be glorified, now I will be exalted;
now you will see, now you will be ashamed. The strength of your spirit will be in vain; fire will devour you.
And the peoples will be burned like thorns in the field, scattered and burned.
Those who are far off will hear what I have done, and those who are near will know my might."
The lawless who were in Zion have departed, and trembling has seized the ungodly. Who will tell you that a fire is blazing? Or who will tell you of the eternal place?

The one who walks in righteousness and speaks of the way of uprightness, who hates lawlessness and falsehood, and has kept his hands away from bribes, and has stopped his ears so as not to hear a false judgment of blood, and has shut his eyes so as not to see falsehood:
he will dwell in the high cave of the strong rock. Bread will be given to him, and his water will be sure.
You will see the King in glory, and your eyes will see the land from afar.
And your soul will meditate on fear. Where are the scribes? Or where are the counselors? Where is the one who was counting those who go about [?]?
The small and the great, to whom he did not speak, nor with a voice from on high, so that he would not hear. The people has been brought to nothing, and the one who hears has no understanding.

Behold, Zion, the city of our salvation; your eyes shall see Jerusalem. O rich city, tents that shall not be shaken, and the pegs of its tent shall not be moved for all time, nor shall its cords be broken.
For the name of the Lord is great upon you. You shall have a place where there are rivers and broad valleys; you shall not go by this way. Let your ships not sail.
For my God is great; he shall not pass me by. The Lord is our judge, the Lord is our ruler, the Lord is our king, the Lord is our savior, and he himself will save us.

Your cords have broken, because they did not hold firm. Your tent pole has bent. Your tent poles will not be spread out [?]. It will not raise a signal until you are given up to be plundered. Now, therefore, many lame people will carry off plunder.
And the people who dwell in it will not say, "We are weary," for their sin has been forgiven them.
Draw near, you nations, and hear; and you rulers, [?]. Let the earth hear, and those who are on it, the world and the people, and those who dwell on it.
For the wrath of the Lord is upon all the nations, and his anger is upon all their number, to destroy them and to give them over to slaughter.
Their wounded and their dead shall be thrown out, and their stench shall rise up.

The mountains shall be soaked with their blood, and the heaven shall be rolled up like the parchment of a book. All the stars shall fall as a leaf falls from the vine, and as a leaf falls from the fig tree.
For my sword has been made drunk in the heavens. Behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and in judgment upon the people doomed to destruction.

The sword of the Lord is filled with blood and has grown fat with fat, with the blood of goats and lambs, and with the fat of calves and rams. For the Lord has a sacrifice in Bozrah and a great slaughter in Idumea.
The rich shall fall with them, and the rams and the calves. The land shall be made drunk with their blood, and the soil shall be filled with their fat,
for it is the day of the Lord's judgment, and the year of recompense for the judgment of Zion.
Its streams shall be turned into pitch, and its land into sulphur, and its land shall be like burning pitch
night and day, and it shall not be quenched for all time. Its smoke shall rise up on high, and it shall lie desolate from generation to generation, and for a long time. No one shall pass through it.
Birds and hedgehogs shall dwell in it, and ravens shall live in it. The measuring line of desolation shall be stretched out over it, and onocentaurs shall live in it.
It shall have no rulers, for its kings, its rich men and its rulers have been given over to destruction.
Thorny trees shall spring up in its cities, and they shall be rough places [?] where dragons live, and a dwelling place of sirens.
Demons and onocentaurs shall meet one another, and one shall cry out to its companion. There the onocentaurs shall rest, for they have found a resting place for themselves.
There hedgehogs have made nests [?], and the earth has carefully raised its young. There the wild beasts have gathered and seen one another's faces,
They came forth by number, and not one of them perished. Each sought its companion, for the Lord commanded them, and his Spirit gathered them.
And he himself will cast their lot, and his hand will divide it among them as pasture for all ages to come, for them to inherit from generation to generation, and they will rest upon it.
Rejoice, O thirsty wilderness, and be glad, O desert, and blossom as the lily blossoms,
and let the deserts of the Jordan spring up and be glad. And the glory of Lebanon has been given to it, and the honour of Carmel; and my people shall see the glory of the Lord and the majesty of God.
Be strong, you weakened hands, and give comfort, you loosened knees.
And say to those who are faint-hearted in mind: Be strong, do not fear. Behold, our God brings judgment, and he will repay. He himself will come and save us.
Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall hear.
Then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the stammering tongue shall speak plainly.

For water has broken forth in the wilderness, and a river in the thirsty land. And the waterless land shall become marshland, and in the thirsty land there shall be a spring of waters. There the birds shall rejoice, and there shall be a dwelling of serpents [or dragons], and reeds, and marshes.

And there shall be a cleansed road there, and it shall be called the holy way. No unclean person shall pass along it, and there shall be no way of uncleanness there. But those who were scattered shall walk along it, and they shall not go astray.
And there shall be no lion there, nor shall any evil beast go up on it, nor be found there. But the redeemed shall walk on it,

those gathered by the Lord. They shall return and come to Zion with joy and gladness, with everlasting joy upon their heads; for praise is upon their heads, and gladness and joy shall overtake them. Pain, sorrow and sighing have fled away.
And it came to pass in the fourteenth year of the reign of Hezekiah that Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, came up against the fortified cities of Judea and seized them.
And the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a great army. And he stood by the conduit of the waters of the upper pool, on the road to the fuller's field.
And Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the steward, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, went out to him.
And Rabshakeh said to them: Say to Hezekiah, Thus says the king of Assyria: In whom do you trust?
Is war waged with counsel and the words of the lips? And now, in whom do you trust, that you have rebelled against me?
Behold, you trust in that staff of broken reed, Egypt, which pierces the hand of any man who leans on it and goes right through it. Such is Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and all who trust in him.

If you say, 'We trust in the Lord our God', is he not the very one whose high places and altars Hezekiah destroyed? And Hezekiah commanded all Judea, saying: You shall worship him before this one altar only, in Jerusalem.
And now come and submit to my lord, the king of the Assyrians, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able to put riders of your own on them.
And how then are you able to turn back the faces of those petty local rulers? They are servants of my lord. And you trust in the Egyptians, and in their chariots and their horsemen.
Now then, have we come up against this land to fight you without the Lord God? The Lord God told me to go out and destroy this land.

And Eliakim, Shebna and Joah said to Rabshakeh: "Speak to your servants in Persian, in Assyrian, for we understand it. Do not speak to us in the Jewish language. What do you gain by saying this in the Jewish language in the hearing of this people who are sitting on the walls?"

Rabshakeh answered and said to them: "Is it to your lord, or to you, that my lord has sent me to speak these words? Is it not to that people who sit on the walls, so that they will not be [?], and will eat their own dung and drink their own urine together with you?"
And Rabshakeh the cupbearer stood in a high place in full view of the city. He cried out with a loud voice in the Jewish language and said: "Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria.
Thus says the king: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you with words, for he is not able to deliver you.
And do not let Hezekiah tell you, 'God will deliver you, and this city will not be given into the hands of the king of Assyria.'

Do not listen to Hezekiah. Thus says the king of Assyria: If you want terms of peace, come out to me. Then you will rejoice over your own fruit, and each of you will eat from his own vine and from his own fig tree, and drink water from his own cistern,
until I come and take you away to a land that is like this land of yours: a land of wheat and of wine, of bread and of vineyards.
Now do not let Hezekiah deceive you by telling you, 'Your God will deliver you.' Did any of the gods of the nations deliver its own country from the hands of the king of Assyria?
Where is the god of Hamath, and of Arpad? And where is the god of the city of Sepharvaim? Were they able to deliver Samaria from my hand?
Which of the gods of all these nations has delivered its land from my hand? How then will that God of Israel deliver Jerusalem from my hands?"
And they were silent, and no one answered him a word. For King Hezekiah had commanded, "None of you is to answer him anything, not a single word."
And Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the steward, Shebna, the scribe of the people, and Joah son of Asaph, Hezekiah's recorder, went in with their garments torn and told him these words of Rabshakeh.
And when Hezekiah heard this, he tore his garments, put on sackcloth, and went up to the temple of the Lord.
And he sent Eliakim the steward, Shebna the scribe and the elders of the priests, dressed in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
And they said to him: "Thus says Hezekiah: This present day is a day of distress and reproach, of rebuke and wrath. For the pains of childbirth have come, but there is no strength to give birth."

May the Lord your God hear these words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria, his lord, sent to reproach the living God with the words that he spoke, which the Lord your God himself heard. And now arise and pray to the Lord your God for this remnant.
And the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah the prophet.

And Isaiah said to them: "Say this to your lord: Thus says the Lord: Do not be afraid of the words that you heard from that cupbearer, whom the king of Assyria sent as a messenger to reproach with words, which the Lord my God heard.

Behold, I will put into him a terrifying thought, so that he will hear a report from far off and turn back quickly to his own land. And he will fall by the sword in his own land and be crushed there."

And when that cupbearer turned back from there, he caught up with and found the king of Assyria. For he had set out from Lachish and arrived, and had besieged and surrounded the city of the Libnites, Libnah.

And there the king of the Assyrians heard that Tirhakah, the king of India, had come out and, having been sent forth and spread out, had filled his land in order to surround him. And when he heard this, he at once gathered himself, [?] (possibly "was afraid"), set out, and went away quickly to his own land. And again he sent messengers there to Hezekiah, the king of Judea, and said:
"Say this to Hezekiah, king of Judea: Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying that Jerusalem will not be given into the hands of the king of Assyria.
Surely you have heard what the kings of Assyria did to every land: how they laid them waste, slaughtered them, and destroyed them. So now, will you be delivered from my hands?
Did the gods of those nations deliver them, whom our fathers slaughtered: the land of Gozan, and Haran, and Rezeph, and the sons of Nadan who lived in the land of Teman?
Now where are the kings of Hamath and of Arpad? And where are the kings of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and of Ivvah?"
And King Hezekiah took the letter from the hands of the messengers and read it. And Hezekiah went into the temple of the Lord God and spread the letter out before the Lord God.
Hezekiah bowed down on his knees before the Lord God and said:
"O Lord God of hosts, God of Israel, you who sit upon the cherubim, you alone are God over all the rulers of the earth. You made heaven and earth.
Incline your ear and hear, O Lord, and hear these words of King Sennacherib, which he sent to reproach the living God.
And truly the kings of Assyria have laid waste every land and their countries.
And they burned their idols with fire, for they were not gods but were the work of human hands, of wood and of stone, and so they destroyed them.
But now you, O Lord our God, deliver us from his hands, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are God."
And Isaiah son of Amoz was sent to Hezekiah and said to him: "Thus says the Lord God of Israel: I have heard your prayer, when you prayed to me about Sennacherib, the king of the Assyrians."
This is the word that the Lord God spoke concerning him: The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and scorned you. The daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you.
Now consider: whom have you reproached, or whom have you provoked to anger? Against whom have you raised your voice, without lifting your eyes on high toward the Holy One of Israel?

For through your messengers you reproached the Lord your God. You said: “With the great multitude of my chariots I have gone up to the heights of the mountains and reached the farthest parts of Lebanon. I have cut down its tall firs and pines and the beauty of its cypresses, and I have entered the heights of the forest of Carmel.
I have laid bridges, broken up the waters and all the gathered waters.”
Did you not hear long ago what I did? I ordained it in the first days. But now I have decreed the destruction of mighty nations in their strongholds, and of the inhabitants of strong cities.
I let them go from my hand, and they dried up. They became like dry hay on the [?] (roof), and like withered grass before it has grown strong.
And now I myself know the places where you rest. I know your going out and your coming in.

Your wrath, with which you raged against me, and your bitterness have reached me. So now I will put a ring in your nose and a bridle in your jaws, and I will turn you back by the road on which you came.
And this shall be a sign for you: this year you shall eat what you have sown, and in the second year what remains of it. But in the third year sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
And the remnant shall be in Judea. Their roots shall spread downward, and they shall bear seed above.
For those who remain shall come from Jerusalem, and those who escape from Mount Zion. The zeal of the Lord Almighty will do this.

Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts about the king of the Assyrians: He shall not enter this city. He shall not shoot an arrow at it, bring a shield against it, or set up a siege rampart against it.
By the road on which he came, by that same road he shall go back, and he shall not enter this city, said the Lord. Thus says the Lord:
I will stand over that city to save it for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.
And an angel went out from God and struck the camp of the Assyrians, killing one hundred and eighty-five thousand men. When they rose at dawn and looked, they found all those bodies dead.
And the messenger turned back from there. [?] Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, went away from there. He came and settled in Nineveh.

He had gone into the temple of Asadrach (Nisroch) to worship his idols. There his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him and killed him with the sword. They fled to the mountains of Armenia, and his son Esarhaddon (Nakordan) put on the crown in his place.

At that time King Hezekiah fell ill with a mortal sickness. The prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz, came to him and said to him: Thus says the Lord God: Set your house in order, for you are going to die and will not live.
When Hezekiah heard this, he turned his face to the wall. He prayed to the Lord
and said: Remember me, O Lord, for I have walked before you in truth, and with a whole heart I have done what is pleasing in your sight. And Hezekiah wept bitterly in repentance.
And the word of the Lord came to Isaiah, and said to him:

"Go quickly to Hezekiah and say to him: Thus says the Lord, the God of your father David: I have heard the voice of your prayer and I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add fifteen years to your days.
And I will deliver you and your city from the hands of the king of Assyria, and I will be the protector over that city of yours.
And this shall be the sign from the Lord that God will fulfil the word that he has spoken:

Behold, I will turn back the shadow of the sun on those steps, where the shadow has gone down ten steps on the house of your father Ahaz; I will turn the shadow of the sun back ten steps." And the shadow of the sun went back ten steps, the same steps by which it had gone down.
The prayer of Hezekiah, king of Judah, when he fell sick and recovered from his sickness.
I said, in the height of my days: I shall go to the gates of Hell; I shall leave behind all my remaining years.
And I said: I shall no longer see the salvation of God on the land of the living; I shall no longer see a man together with those who dwell with me.

I have been cut off from my kindred. From now on I have left it, and what remained of my life [?] has gone out and departed. My soul has gone far from me, like someone who would pull down a pitched tent; [so] my soul [?]. And it was like a woven web [?] drawn near to be cut off.
In that day I was given over from dawn on, as into the hands of a lion; so he ground and crushed my bones, for from dawn until evening I was given over.
Like a swallow, so I chirped, and like a dove, so I moaned, for my eyes failed to see.
I looked up to the height of heaven, to the Lord my God, who delivered me and took away the pain of my body from me.
O Lord, for this it was told to you; you roused my mind, you brought back my spirit. I was comforted and I lived. Behold, my bitterness has turned to peace,
and you delivered my soul, so that I should not perish; you cast all my sins away from me,
for those who are in Hell will not praise you, nor will the dead bless you, nor will those who go down into the pit hope in your truth and your mercy;
but the living will bless you, as I do, for from now on I will beget children who will tell of this, your righteousness and your mercy.
O Lord, God of my salvation, I will not cease to bless you with a new song all the days of my life, before the Lord and the house of God.
And Isaiah the prophet said to Hezekiah: "Take a cake of figs and crush it, and lay it on your wound, and you will recover."
And Hezekiah said: "Is this the sign that I shall go up to the house of God?"

At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent envoys, letters, and gifts to Hezekiah, for he had heard that he had fallen sick almost to death and had recovered from his sickness.

And Hezekiah rejoiced at the coming of those envoys. He led them in with joy and showed them his treasure-houses: of silver and of gold, of stacte, of incense and of ointments, and all the storehouses of provisions and of wealth, and everything that was laid up among his treasures. There was nothing in his house or in all his dominion that Hezekiah did not show them.

And Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, "What do these men say? And where have they come to you from?" Hezekiah answered and said, "They have come to me from a far country, from the land of the Babylonians."

And Isaiah said to him, "What did they see in your house?" Hezekiah answered and said to him, "They saw everything that was in my house. There is nothing in my house that they did not see, even my treasures."
And Isaiah said to him, "Now hear the word of the Lord Almighty:

Behold, the days are coming when they will carry off everything that is in your house, and all that your fathers have gathered up to this day, and they will take it into the land of Babylon, and nothing will be left, said the Lord.
And they will also take away some of your sons whom you have begotten, and they will make them eunuchs in the house of the king of Babylon."
Hezekiah answered and said to Isaiah, "Good and fine is the word that the Lord has spoken. Let there be peace and righteousness in my days; but in the days of my offspring, as he wills."
Comfort, comfort my people, said the Lord.
Priests, speak to the heart of Jerusalem; comfort her, for her humiliation has been fulfilled and her sins are forgiven, for she has received from the hand of the Lord double recompense for her sins.
The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the ways of the Lord, make straight the places of the Lord my God.
Every valley shall be filled up, and every high mountain and hill shall be made low, and all the rough places shall be turned into easy ones, and the rugged places shall become plains.
And the glory of the Lord shall appear, and all flesh shall see the salvation of God, for the Lord has spoken.
A voice said, "Cry out!" And I said, "What shall I cry?" All flesh is grass, and all the glory of man is like the flower of the grass.
The grass has withered, and its flower has fallen,
but the word of the Lord abides forever.

Go up onto a high mountain, you who bring good tidings to Zion; lift up your voice with strength, you who bring good tidings to Jerusalem. Lift it up, do not be afraid; say to the cities of Judah: Behold, our God!
Behold, the Lord comes with strength, and his arm with dominion. Behold, his reward is with him, and his works are before him.
Like a shepherd he will tend his flock, and with his arm he will gather the lambs, and he will comfort those that are with young.
Who has measured the waters in his handful, and heaven with his span, and the whole earth with his hand's breadth? Who has weighed the mountains in a balance and the hills on the beam of the scales?
For who has known the mind of the Lord, or who has been his counselor, to set him on the right track? Or who has counseled him and made things known to him?
Or who has shown him judgment, or who has taught him the way of understanding?
If all the nations are counted as drops from a bucket, and as the tipping of a scale, and are counted as spittle from the mouth.
And Lebanon is not enough for burning, and all the four-footed beasts are not enough for a sacrifice.
And all the nations are as nothing, and are counted as nothing.
Now to whom have you likened the Lord, or to what likeness have you likened him?
Surely a craftsman did not make him into an image, or a goldsmith blow gold in furnaces and, by the knowledge of his own skill, fashion him as a standing figure in the likeness of an image?
A craftsman picks out wood that does not rot from the forest, and with the wisdom of his skill he sets it up as an idol. He [?] it with all kinds of cunning so that it cannot be moved.
Now do you not hear, and have you not understood? Was it not told to you from the beginning? Do you know who established the foundations of the earth,

or who holds the circle of the earth, with those who dwell on it like locusts; who set up the heavens like a vault and stretched them out like tents, as dwellings, and established the earth to be dwelt upon,
and brought the rulers low as nothing, together with their dominion, and made the earth upon nothing?
For they did not sow, nor plant a shoot, nor did their roots spread out over the earth. The wind blew on them and they withered, and the gust gathered them up like chaff.
Now to what likeness have you likened me, that I should be exalted? says the Exalted One.

Lift up your eyes on high and see who established all this: who has carried the number of this world one by one, and orders them all by name. By his great glory, by the strength of his arm, not one of them is hidden from you.
Do not say this, Jacob, or why do you say this, Israel? "Who knows?" You said that my ways are hidden from God, and that my God has taken my judgment away from me.

But would you not know by now, had you not heard, that he is eternal forever? The Lord, who established the ends of the earth, does not hunger or grow weary, and there is no searching out his knowledge.
He gives strength to the hungry, and spreads out the thought of desire to the [?].
Young men will hunger, and the strong will grow weary, and their chosen ones will become weak.
But those who wait for the Lord will be renewed in their strength, and they will [?] with new feathers [?] like eagles. They will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not hunger.
Be renewed, be renewed toward me, all you islands, for the rulers will be renewed in their strength. Let them come near and speak, and let them declare judgment together.

Who roused righteousness from the east and called it according to his order? It will go forth and fill the nations; they drove them mad [?]; it will astonish their kings and give their swords to the earth, and their bows will be crushed [?] like chaff.
And they were pursued and turned to flight, and he himself passed along their paths of peace.

Yes, now you say that he does not come. Who created, planned and made all this? Who called it from the eternal generation? I am the Lord God, the first, and I am hereafter, and after that it is still I.
The nations saw me and were afraid; they trembled, and all the ends of the earth were amazed. They set out, drew near to me, surrounded me, came, and all gathered together to me.
And each man resolved in his heart to help his neighbour and his brother, and they spoke to one another.
The carpenter called on the smith to forge, to hammer, to strike with the hammer, to nail, to raise up, to set up and to make it firm, so that it would not be shaken.
But now you, Israel my servant, and Jacob my chosen one, offspring of Abraham, whom I have loved:
you, whom I helped from the ends of the earth, and called from its lookouts, and to whom I said, 'You are my servant.' I chose you and did not cast you away from my hand.
Do not be afraid, for I am with you. Do not go astray, for I am the Lord your God, who strengthened you, and helped you, and took care of you, and kept you with this right arm of my righteousness.
Behold, all your enemies shall be ashamed and put to disgrace, and they shall be as though they had never been. All those who contend against you shall perish.
I will seek them, and you will not find them, those men who insulted you. For they shall be as though they had never been, and those who attacked you shall be no more.
For I am the Lord your God, who took hold of your right hand and said to you, 'Do not be afraid; I am your helper.'
Do not be afraid, my child Jacob, and my little one [?] Israel. I am the Lord your God, who saved you, says God your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.
Behold, I have made you like a cart wheel for threshing, new and shaped like a saw. You will thresh the mountains, grind the hills to powder, and make them like dust.
You will winnow them, and the winds will carry them away, and the clouds will divide them, and the gale will scatter them. But you shall rejoice in the Lord and be glad in the Holy One of Israel.

And the poor, the hungry and the needy shall rejoice. They seek water and do not find it, and their tongues are dried up with thirst. I, the Lord God, will hear them; I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
Instead I will open rivers on the mountains, and in the midst of the plains I will make springs flow. I will make the desert into pools of water, and I will send streams into the thirsty land.
In the waterless land I will make the fir and the pine grow, the box tree, the zelkova, and the cypress, and the elm, and the poplar, and the [?], and the myrtle, and the olive tree,
so that they may see and know, and understand and believe together, that the hand of the Lord has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created all this.
Your judgment has drawn near, said the Lord God. Your cases have drawn near, says the Lord God. Your counsels have drawn near, says the King of Jacob.
Now let them come near and tell you what will happen to you, or what the former things were. Speak, and let us understand and know what will be at the end, and tell us the things to come.
Tell us the last things that are to come, and let us know [?], so that you may know whether you are gods. Do good, and do evil, and we will marvel and see together
where you come from and where your making comes from, for abominable ones have chosen you out of the earth.

But I have roused him from the north, and from the sunrise they shall be called by my name. Let them come; the rulers shall gather like a potter's clay, and as the potter treads his clay, so shall they be trodden down.

And who is there who will tell me first, so that you may know, or speak of what has been, so that we may testify that it is true? There is no one who has told you, or who will hear those words of yours.
I will begin with Zion, and I will comfort Jerusalem for its entering in,
for behold, among the nations there is no one, and among their idols there is no one to declare it; and if I ask them, “Who are you?”, they will answer me nothing.
For your makers are false, and your fashioners are vain.
Jacob my servant, I will help him; Israel my chosen, my soul has received him. I will put my spirit upon him, and he shall bring forth judgment to the nations.
He shall not cry out, nor shout aloud, nor shall his voice be heard in the streets.
A bruised reed he shall not break, and a smouldering wick he shall not quench, until he brings forth judgment and the verdict of righteousness.
He shall shine forth and shall not be crushed, until he establishes judgment upon the earth; and in his name the nations shall hope.
Thus says the Lord God, who created the heavens and established them, who made the earth and all that is in it, and gave breath to his people who are upon it, and spirit to all who walk upon it:
I am the Lord God, who have called you in righteousness, and have held your right hand, and strengthened you, and given you as a covenant to the peoples and as a light to the nations,
to open the eyes of the blind, and to bring the bound out of captivity, and out of the prison house those who sit in darkness.
I am the Lord God, and this is my name; my glory I will not give to another, nor this my excellence to carved images.

What was to be told from the beginning, behold, it has come and has arrived; and whatever new thing I speak to you, that too I will declare to you. And before it was yet told, I made it known to you beforehand.

Sing to the Lord a new song, for his dominion (literally, his beginning) is glorified in the heights, and his name is glorious from one end of the earth to the other — you who go down to the sea in ships and sail upon it, the islands and their inhabitants.
Rejoice, O wilderness and you who dwell in it; let the dwellings and the encampments of Kedar rejoice; let the inhabitants of the rock rejoice; let them shout from the tops of the mountains.
Let them give glory to God, and declare his might in the islands.
The Lord God of hosts has set out, and comes to rouse up battle, to stir up zeal, to blow the trumpet, to shout aloud and to go out against his enemies with great might.

I have kept silent from the beginning; shall I keep silent now as well? Now I will keep silent no longer. I bore it, even though I endured like a woman in childbirth. Now I will make it manifest and astonish everything all at once.
I will dry up the hills and make them desolate, and I will dry up all their grass all at once. I will set island beside island out of their rivers, and I will dry up all its pools [?].

And I will lead the blind on a way that they did not know, and I will make them walk in places that they did not know. I will turn the darkness into light for them, and the rough land into level ground. These words I will fulfil for them, and I will not forsake them.
But they turned back on their own tracks. Let those who trust in idols be put to shame with great shame, those who say to their cast images, "You are our gods."
Woe, you deaf, hear! And you blind, open your eyes and see!
Now who is blind to me, if not my people? Or who are the deaf, if not those who rule over them? And the servants of God have become blind.
You have seen many times, and we did not take heed; your ears were opened, and you did not hear.
The Lord our God took counsel so that you might be justified and might exalt his praise.

He looked and saw how the people had been plundered and despoiled: for a snare had been laid in all the treasuries, and all the temples together were full of stumbling-blocks. They became a prey, and there was no one to rescue them. You were handed over to captivity, and there was no one to say, "Give them back."
Who is there among you who will understand this and will listen to what is to come hereafter?
Who handed Jacob over to be plundered and Israel to be taken captive? Was it not God himself, against whom they sinned? For they did not want to walk in his ways or to listen to his law.

And he sent and brought upon them the wrath of his anger, and overcame them in war. Those who set things on fire stood all around them, and they did not know it; they did not recognize one another, nor did they take this to heart, and it blazed up among them.
And now, behold, thus says the Lord God, who made you, Jacob, and who created you, Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you, and I have called you by my name: you are mine.
If you pass through many waters, I am with you, and the rivers shall never overwhelm you; and if you pass through fire, you shall not be burned, and its flame shall not burn you,
for I am the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel, who saves you. Behold, I have made Egypt an exchange for you, and the land of India and the city of Syene I have made wholly a payment for you.
Since you became precious in my eyes, you were glorified, and I loved you; and now I will give many men in exchange for you, and rich rulers as a payment for your life.
Do not fear, for I am with you: I will bring your offspring from the east, and I will gather you from the west.
I will command the north to gather them, and say to the south, "Do not hold them back." Bring them, gather my sons from a far-off land and my daughters from the ends of the earth,
all who are called by my name, for I prepared him for my glory, and I created him, and I made him,
and I brought him out like a blind people; their eyes are likewise blind, and their ears do not hear.

All the nations have gathered together, and rulers will gather from among them. Who will tell them this, or what was from the beginning? Who will make you hear? Let them bring their witnesses and be proved right; let them hear and speak the truth.

Be my witnesses, and I am a witness for you, says the Lord God, and so is my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he who was from the beginning. Before me there was no other god, and after me there shall be none.
I am God, and there is no saviour apart from me.
I told you, and I saved you. I am the one who openly reproached you, and you could not show me another god. You yourselves are my witnesses, and I am the Lord God.
From the beginning I am, and there is no other who can take you out of my hands. I will act, and who will turn it back?

Thus says the Lord God, your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: For your sake I will send to Babylon, and I will rouse them up and throw all of them into panic as fugitives, and the race of the Chaldeans will be held fast in ships.
I am the Lord God, your Holy One, who appointed for you the King of Israel.
Thus says the Lord God, who made a way through the sea and opened up paths through the mighty waters,
who brought out chariots and horses and a great and mighty host; but they lay down and will not rise again; they were put out like a wick that has been quenched.
Do not remember the former things, and what happened before — why do you take it to heart?
For behold, I will make something new, which will shine forth even now, and you will know it. I will make a way in the wilderness, and rivers will appear in the waterless land.

The wild beasts of the field will bless me, and the female [?] and the daughters of the wild creatures [?]. For I have given water in the wilderness, and have made rivers spring up in the waterless land, so that my chosen people may drink.
And you, the people whom I acquired for myself, shall tell of my excellent deeds.
It was not now that I called you, Jacob, nor did I make you toil, Israel.
You did not bring me sheep for your sacrifices, nor did you glorify me with your offerings. I did not make you serve me with offerings, nor did I make you toil for incense.
You did not buy me incense with silver, nor did my heart long for the fat of your sacrifices. Instead you always stood before me with your sins and appeared before me with your iniquities.
I, I am the one who blots out your iniquities for my own sake, and I will no longer remember your sins.
But remember, and let us be judged together. Tell your iniquity first, so that you may be justified.
Your fathers sinned first, and your rulers acted lawlessly against me.
Your rulers defiled my sanctuary, so I handed Jacob over to destruction and Israel to reproach.
But now hear, Jacob my servant, and Israel whom I have chosen.
Thus says the Lord God, who made you and who formed you from your mother's womb: I will help you. Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant, and Israel my beloved, whom I have chosen.
For I will give water to the thirsty, to those who walk in a waterless land, and I will put my spirit upon your offspring and my blessings upon your children.
And they will spring up like grass among waters, and like willows beside running streams of water.
One will say, 'I belong to God,' and another will call himself by the name of Jacob. And another will write with his own hand, 'I belong to God,' and will cry out in the name of Israel.
Thus says the Lord God, the King of Israel, the eternal God who redeemed him: I am the beginning and I am the end, and apart from me there is no other god.
Who else is like me, the Lord? Let him stand up and call out, and declare it, and set it out before me, since the time I made man for ever; and let them tell you the things to come before they come.

Do not hide from me, and do not go astray. From the beginning you heard [?]. Can you not tell me? Now you are my witnesses. Is there anyone besides me, another god? And even then there were none of them,

those who fashioned vain things and carved a useless idol. For all who are vain walk by the desire of their own mind, and these things were of no profit to them. And you too are witnesses against those who do not see and do not understand, so that they may be ashamed,
those who fashion the fashioned thing, the carved and the engraved, to no use.

And all who were made by it withered, and all who fashion idols and carve that useless thing were put to shame, and all those from whom they came withered. The deaf among men, let them all gather and stand together. Let them be ashamed before one another, and let them all be put to shame together. For they are craftsmen, and they are men from among men.

For the craftsman brought out his tool, sharpened the axe, and hewed with it. He shaped it with a chisel and cut it out, and with the strength of his arm he set it up. He grows hungry and thirsty and weak, and cannot drink water.

The craftsman chose the wood from the forest. He weighed it by measure and fashioned it after the likeness of the form of an image. He laid it out with a chisel, and fastened it with glue into the image of a man. He set it up, and with the comeliness of a man's form he fixed it firmly in his house.
That wood, cypress or linden, oak or elm, which the Lord planted and made to grow by the abundance of the rains,

and prepared for people to burn. A man took it, burned it and warmed himself, cooked food with it, and was filled. Then he took the remnant of that wood, made idols, set them up, and bowed down to them. Now then, before the thing he made into an idol by himself he has fallen down, and he bows down to it.

For part of that wood the furnace burned up, and with part of that wood he made bread, and with part of that wood he roasted meat. He ate, was filled, was satisfied, and warmed himself, and said: "Aha, I am warm!"

And part of the leftover wood he hewed, cut out, carved, and made into an idol, and he called it god. He has fallen down and bows down to it, rolls on the ground before it, and says: "Save me, for you are my god."
They did not understand with their mind, for their eyes turned away from seeing, and they were dulled [?] in the thoughts of their heart.

They did not consider in their heart, and they did not reason with their understanding. They could not call to mind that part of that wood they burned with fire, and with it they baked bread, and on its coals they roasted meat and ate it, and the remnant of that wood they made into an idol and set up as an image, and they bow down to it and say: "Save us."
Behold, know now that their heart is ash. They have gone astray, and none of them could save his own soul. Take thought, beware. Who knows? Say that there is no falsehood in our hands.
Remember these things, Jacob and Israel, for you are my servant. I acquired you for myself; you are my servant. And you too, Israel, do not forget me.
Behold, I will blot out all your iniquities like clouds, and I will take all your sins far from you like mist. Return to me, and I will redeem you.

Rejoice, you heavens, and let the earth be glad, for God has had mercy on Israel. Blow the trumpet, you foundations of the earth; cry out, you mountains and hills, with all the woods, for God has redeemed Jacob, and Israel shall be glorified.
Thus says the Lord, who redeemed you and formed you from your mother's womb: I am the Lord, who makes and orders all these things. I alone stretched out the heavens, and I established the earth.

Who else, then, shall bring it to nothing? I am the one who brought to nothing the signs of the ventriloquists and the divinations from the heart. I turned the wise backward, and made their counsels foolish.

And I will confirm the word of my servant, and make the counsels of his messengers come true. I am the one who said to Jerusalem, 'Be built,' and to the city of Judea, 'Be inhabited,' and I raised up all its desolate places.
I am the one who said to the abyss, 'Be laid waste,' and I dried up all your rivers.
I am the one who said to Cyrus, 'Be wise,' and he shall carry out all my will. I am the one who said to Jerusalem, 'Be built,' and I will raise up the temple of my holiness.

Thus says the Lord God to my anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have held, to subdue the nations before him; and I will shatter the strength of kings, to open the gates before him, and the cities shall not be hard for him to take.
I will go before you and level the mountains, and I will grind to pieces the gates of bronze and break the bars of iron.
And I will give you the treasures of darkness, and I will open to you the hidden things, concealed and unseen, so that you may know that I am the Lord God, who called you by name, the God of Israel.
For the sake of Jacob my servant, and for the sake of Israel my chosen one, I called you by my name and accepted you, but you did not know me.
For I am the Lord your God, and there is no other God besides me. I strengthened you, and you did not understand,
so that they may know, from the rising of the sun and from its setting, that there is no other God besides me. I am the Lord God, and there is no other.
I prepared light and made darkness; I made peace and created evil. I am the Lord God, who made all these things.

Rejoice, you heavens above, and let the clouds sprinkle righteousness. Let the earth sprout mercy, and let righteousness spring up together with it. I am the Lord your God, who created you and made you better.

I prepared you like a potter's clay. Will the plowman plow the earth all day long? Or will the clay say to the potter, 'What are you making?' or 'What are you doing?' And will the thing made say, 'You have no hands'? Or will the created thing talk back to its own creator?
Woe to the one who says to his father, 'Why did you beget me?' and to his mother, 'Why were you in labor with me?'
For thus says the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel, who created him, who made the things that are to come: Ask me about my sons, and give me commands concerning the works of my hands.
I made the earth and man upon it. With my hand I established the heavens, and I myself by my command set all the stars in order.

I have raised him up in righteousness to reign, and all his ways are straight. He shall build my city and bring back the captives of my people, not for ransom and not for bribes, said the Lord God of hosts.

Thus says the Lord God of hosts: The land of Egypt has toiled, and the merchants of India and the Sabaeans, men of wealth, shall come over to you and stand beneath you. They shall serve you and follow after you; bound in fetters on their hands they shall come to you, and they shall bow down to you and make their vows to you.
For God is with you, and there is no other God besides you. You are God, and we did not know God, the Savior of Israel, and we did not recognize you.
Let all his enemies be ashamed and disgraced, and let them go about in shame. Islands, renew yourselves before me.
For Israel has been saved by the Lord with an everlasting salvation. They shall not be ashamed or disgraced for all the ages of time.

Thus says the Lord God who made the heavens. This is the God who created the earth and made it. This is he who created it, and he did not make it for nothing; he made and created it to be lived in and built upon. I am the Lord, and there is no other.

I did not speak to you in secret, or in a dark land. Nowhere did I tell the descendants of Jacob that you should seek after worthless things. I am the Lord, who speaks righteousness and tells you the truth.

Gather together and come, and take counsel together, you who have been saved from among the gentiles. Those who carried up and brought the hewn wood, the carved [?] wood, did not understand. They still bow down to it and call it a god, and it cannot save them.

Who knows? Will they tell you anything [?] about God? Let them come and draw near, and let them all learn together who made this heard from the beginning, from that day, before it was told to you. I am God, and there is no other besides me, righteous and a Savior; there is none besides me.
Turn to me and be saved, you who are at the ends of the earth. I am God, and there is no other besides me.
I swear by myself that righteousness shall go out of my mouth, and my words shall not turn back. For to me every knee shall bow, and every tongue shall swear by the true God.
And they shall say, 'Righteousness and glory shall come to him.' And all who separate themselves from the Lord shall be ashamed.
But all the descendants shall be justified, and they shall be glorified in God.
Bel has fallen, and Dagon is shattered. Their carved images have been given to wild beasts and cattle. They carry them bound like a burden that wears out the one who carries it.
They do not have the strength to carry them; they are hungry and worn out together. They cannot rescue anyone from battle, and they themselves are carried away captive.
Listen to me, house of Jacob, and all the remnant of Israel, you who were chosen from your mother's womb and taught from childhood.
Until old age I am he, and until you grow old I am still he. I carry you. I made you, and I will have mercy on you; I will lift you up and save you.
To whom have you compared me? See and consider, you who have gone astray,
Those who pour out gold from the [?] and weigh silver on the beam of a balance hire a goldsmith. They make idols with their hands, and they bow down and worship them.

They lift them onto their shoulders and go off. If they set them down, the idols stay where they are and cannot move. If anyone cries out to them, they do not hear, and they cannot save anyone from evil.
Remember this and groan. Repent, you who have gone astray, and turn back in your hearts,
and remember the first things of old, for I am God, and there is no other besides me.

I am the one who declared the first things and the last before they came to be, and all of it will be fulfilled together. I said that all my counsel shall stand, and everything I have planned I will do.
I call a bird from the east, and from a far country those about whom I have planned. I have spoken, I have brought him, and I have made his ways prosper.
Listen to me, you who have lost heart, you who are far from righteousness.
My righteousness has come near. It will not be delayed, and the salvation that comes from me will not linger. I have placed salvation in Zion, for Israel's glory.

Come down and sit on the ground, virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground, for there is no throne for you. Sit in darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans, for you will no longer be called tender, delicate, and pampered, you queen of the Chaldeans.
Take millstones and grind flour. Take off your veil. Uncover your gray hairs. Gather up your skirt. Bare your legs. Cross the rivers.
Your shame will be revealed, and your disgrace will be seen. For I have taken your justice from you and removed it far away. I will no longer hand you over to men,
says the one who redeemed you, the Lord God of hosts; his name is the Holy One of Israel.
Now sit in sorrow and go into the darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. From now on you will no longer be called the strength of crowns.

For I was angry, and because of my people I gave them into your hands, because they had defiled my inheritance. But you did not show mercy to a single one of them. On the old you laid a very heavy yoke.
You said, 'I will rule forever.' You did not take these things to heart, and you did not remember your end.

But now hear this, you pampered one, who sit without a care, trusting in yourself and self-confident [?], who said in your heart, 'I am, and there is no one else [?]. I will not sit as a widow, nor will I [?] at all.'

Now both of these things will come upon you suddenly, in a single day: widowhood and orphanhood will come upon you without warning. So stand now with your many sorceries and the great power of your enchantments [?],

and with your hope in your fornications. For you said, 'I am, and there is no one else.' Know that your understanding of these things and your fornications will become your shame. You said in your heart, 'I am, and there is no one else.'

Destruction will come upon you, and you will not sense it. You will fall into a pit, and misery will come upon you, and you will not be able to make yourself clean. Ruin will come upon you suddenly, and you will not know it.
Stand now with your divination and with your many sorceries, which you have learned from your youth, to see whether you can bring yourself any benefit.
You have grown weary in your counsels. Stand now: let the astrologers of heaven, who gaze at the stars, save you. Let them tell you what is about to come upon you.
Behold, they will all be burned up like stubble in fire. They will not deliver themselves from the flame, for you will sit upon coals of fire.
Such were your helpers. You have grown weary with your trading since your youth. Each man has gone astray on his own, but for you there will be no salvation.

Hear this, O house of Israel, you who are called by the name of Israel and who have come out of Judah; you who swear by the name of the Lord God of Israel and are remembered by God, but not in truth or in righteousness;
you who trust in the name of the holy city and rely on the God of Israel. Lord and Almighty is his name.
I told you the former things long ago, from those days. They went out of my mouth, and you heard them. Suddenly I acted, and they came to pass.
I know that you are stubborn: your neck is a sinew of iron, and your forehead is of bronze.
So I told you long ago, before it came upon you. I let you hear it, so that you would not say, 'The idols did this for me,' and so that you would not say, 'The carved and molten images told me.'
You heard this, and you did not understand. But from now on I will also let you hear new things that are about to happen, and you did not know them.
They have come about now, not back then, nor in former days, and you had not heard of them. So do not say, 'Yes, I knew it.'
You neither heard it nor knew it, and I did not open your ears from the beginning, for I knew that you would deal very treacherously and would be called lawless from your mother's womb.
For my name's sake I will show you my wrath, and by my glory I will bring it upon you, so that I may destroy you.
Behold, I have sold you, but not for silver. I have delivered you from the furnace of poverty.
I do this for you for my own sake, because my name is being profaned, and I will not give my glory to another.
Listen to me, Jacob, and Israel, whom I have called. I am the first, and I am forever.
My hand laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand established the heavens. I call them, and they stand up together.
All of them will gather and listen. Who told them this: 'Out of love for you I have done your will, to remove the race of the Chaldeans from Babylon'?
I spoke, and I called him. I brought him, and I made his ways straight.
Come near to me and hear this. From the beginning I have not spoken in secret. When it was happening, I was there. And now the Lord has sent me, and his Spirit.
Thus says the Lord, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am the Lord your God. I have shown you how to find the way in which you should walk.
If you had listened to my commandments, your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
Your descendants would have been like the sand of the sea, and your offspring like the dust of the earth. Even now you will not be wiped out, and your name will not perish before me.
Go out from Babylon, fleeing from the Chaldeans. Proclaim a voice of joy, and let it be heard. Proclaim it to the end of the earth, and say: The Lord has redeemed his servant Jacob.
And he did not leave him thirsty; he called him through the desert, and he will make water flow from the rock for them. The rocks split open and waters flowed, and my people drank.
There is no joy for the ungodly, says the Lord.
Listen to me, you islands, and pay attention, you nations, after a long time: stand, says the Lord. From the womb, from my mother's belly, he called my name,
and he made my mouth like a sharpened sword, and hid me in the shelter of his hand. He set me as a chosen arrow and concealed me in his quiver.
And he said to me: You are my servant, Israel, and in you I will be glorified.
And I said: I have labored in vain; I have spent my strength for emptiness and for nothing. Therefore my judgment is with the Lord, and my toil with my God.

And now thus says the Lord, who formed me from the womb to be his servant, to gather Jacob to him and to bring Israel near to him. And I shall be glorified before the Lord, and my God shall be my strength.

And he said to me: It is a great thing for you, this calling of yours to be my servant, to establish the tribes of Jacob and to gather the scattered ones of Israel. Behold, I have given you as a covenant for the peoples and as a light for the nations, so that you may be a savior to the end of the earth.

Thus says the Lord, your redeemer, the God of Israel: Sanctify the one who is humbled in himself, who is abhorred by the nations, by the servants of rulers. Kings shall see him and rise up, and rulers shall bow down to him for the Lord's sake, for the Holy One of Israel is faithful, and he has chosen you.

Thus says the Lord: In a time of favor I heard you, and in a day of salvation I helped you, and I have given you as a covenant to the nations, to establish the earth and to cause the desolate inheritance to be inherited,
and to say to the prisoners, "Come out," and to those who were in darkness, "Show yourselves." They shall graze along all the roads, and on every place shall be their pasture.
They shall not hunger or thirst, nor shall scorching heat fall on them, nor shall the sun harm them; but he who has mercy on them shall comfort them and lead them to the sources of springs of water.
And I will make all the mountains into a road, and every place into pasture for them.
Behold, these shall come from afar, and some [?] from the north and from the sea, and others from the land of Persia.
Rejoice, O heavens, and let the earth be glad; let the mountains break forth with joy and the hills with righteousness. For God has had mercy on his people and has comforted the lowly of his people.
Zion said: The Lord has forsaken me, and my God has forgotten me.
Will a woman forget her children, so as not to have mercy on the offspring of her womb? But even if a woman should forget them, I will not forget you, said the Lord.
Behold, I have inscribed your walls with my hands, and you are always before my eyes,
and you shall soon be rebuilt by those by whom you were torn down, and those who laid you waste shall soon go out from you.

Lift up your eyes round about and see all your children, for behold, they are gathered and have come to you, and all your offspring surround you. As I live, says the Lord, you shall clothe yourself with them all and adorn yourself with them as a bride puts on her ornaments.
For your waste places, your ruined places and your fallen places will now be too narrow for those who live there, and those who swallowed you up will be far from you.
For your sons, the ones you had lost, will say in your ears: "Make the place wider for us to live in, because this place is too narrow for us."
And you will say in your heart: "Who has borne me these? For I was childless and a widow, an exile and bereft. Who has brought these up for me? I was left alone; where were these?"

Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will lift up my hand among the nations, and I will raise up my sign toward the islands. They will bring your sons in their bosom, and your daughters will be carried on their shoulders.

Kings will be your nurses, and princesses your nursing mothers. They will bow down to you with their faces to the ground and lick the dust under your feet. And you will know that I am the Lord, and those who wait for me will not be put to shame.
Will anyone take the spoil from a giant? And if anyone takes captives unjustly, will he be saved?
Thus says the Lord: If anyone takes a giant captive, he will take spoil; and whoever takes from the strong, will he be saved? But I will judge your cause, and I will save your sons.

Those who oppress you will eat their own flesh, and they will drink their own blood like new wine and become drunk. And all flesh will know that I am the Lord, who saved you and helped you, your strengthener, O Jacob.

Thus says the Lord: Did I write a bill of divorce for your mother, by which I sent her away? Or to whom was I in debt, that I sold you? Behold, because of your sins you were [?sold], and because of your lawlessness I sent your mother away.

For I came, and there was no one; I called, and there was no one who would listen. Is my hand now unable to redeem? Or do I have no power to deliver? Behold, by my rebuke I will make the sea desolate, and I will turn rivers into wilderness. Their fish will dry up for lack of water, and they will die of thirst.
I will clothe the heavens in darkness, and I will make their garment as nothing.
The Lord God has given me a tongue of knowledge, so that I may know the word in its season. He made me watchful at daybreak for counsel, and at dawn he gave me an ear to hear.
And the instruction of the Lord opened my ears, and I was not disobedient, nor did I contradict.
I gave my back to scourging and my cheeks to slapping, and I did not turn my face away from the shame of spitting.
And the Lord became my helper. Therefore I was not put to shame; instead I made my face like a firm rock, and I knew that I would not be put to shame.
For the one who vindicates me is near. Who is my adversary at law? Let him stand up against me. And who is my judge? Let him come near to me.
Behold, the Lord is my helper; who is there to do me harm? Behold, all of you will wear out like garments, and the moth will eat you up.
Who among you fears the Lord? Let him listen to the voice of his servant. You who walk in darkness and have no light among you: trust in the name of the Lord, and lean firmly on our God.
Behold, all of you kindle fire and make the flame strong. Now walk in the light of your fire and in the flame that you have kindled. This shall come to you from me: you shall lie down in sorrow.
Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness and seek the Lord: look to the solid rock from which you were hewn, and to the deep pit from which you were dug.
Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who bore you, for he was one, and I called him, and blessed him, and loved him, and multiplied him.

And you, Zion, I will now comfort, and I will comfort all your desolate places, and I will make all your deserts like a paradise of delight, and its western parts like the paradise of God. Joy and gladness shall be found in it, thanksgiving and the voice of praise.
Listen to me, listen to me, and you kings, give ear to me, for my law shall go forth from me, and my judgment as a light to the nations.
My righteousness draws near quickly, and my salvation shall go forth like light, and the nations shall hope in my arm. The thickets wait for me, and they shall hope in my arm.

Lift up your eyes to heaven and look at the earth, for heaven has been made firm like smoke, and the earth shall grow old like a garment. And its inhabitants shall perish just like these, but my salvation shall be forever, and my righteousness shall not fail.
Listen to me, you who know justice, my people, in whose hearts my law is: do not be afraid of the reproach of men, and do not be weakened by their contempt.
For as garments grow old over many seasons, and as wool is eaten by moths, so my righteousness shall endure forever, and my salvation from generation to generation.
Awake, awake, Jerusalem, and put on the strength of your arm; awake as in the beginning of days. Are you not the one
who laid waste the sea and the many waters of the abyss, who made the depth of the sea a road to cross over for those who were delivered

and redeemed? For by the Lord they shall return, and they shall come to Zion with joy and everlasting gladness, for praise shall be upon their heads, and gladness shall overtake them. Pain, sorrow, and sighing have fled away.
I am the one who comforts you, I myself. Know what you were: you were afraid of mortal man, and of a son of man of foreign seed, who wither like grass.

And you forgot God your maker, who made heaven and founded the earth, and you were afraid continually, all your days, before the face of the wrath of your oppressor, as he planned to carry you off. And now where is the god of your oppressor?
For he shall not be able to stand against your salvation, nor shall he linger.
For I am the Lord your God, who stirred up the sea, and its waves roared. The Lord Almighty is my name.
And I will put my words in your mouth, and I will shelter you under the shade of my hand, by which I set up the heavens and founded the earth, and I said to Zion, "You are my people."
Awake, awake, arise, Jerusalem, you who drank from the hand of the Lord the cup of his wrath; for you have drunk the cup of falling, the chalice of my wrath, and drained it empty.
And there was no one to comfort you among all the children you bore, and there is no one to take you by the hand among all the sons you raised.
These two things have befallen you. Who then will grieve with you? Ruin and destruction, famine and sword. Who then will comfort you?
Your sons, who are themselves faint [?], lay asleep at the head [?] of every road, like a half-boiled beet. They are full of the wrath of the Lord, made weak by the Lord your God.
Therefore hear this, you who are humbled, you who are drunk, but not with wine.
Thus says the Lord your God, who judges his people: Behold, I have taken from your hand the cup of staggering, the chalice of my wrath, and you shall never drink it again.

And I will give it into the hands of those who harmed you and those who humbled you, who said to your soul, "Bow down, so that we may walk over you." And you laid down your back [?] like the ground before all who passed by.
Awake, awake, Zion! Awake, and rouse your strength, O Zion! And you too, Jerusalem, holy city, put on your glory. From now on the uncircumcised and the unclean shall never again pass through you.
Shake the dust off yourself, arise and sit down, Jerusalem. Loose the bond from your neck, O captive daughter of Zion.
For thus says the Lord: You were sold for nothing, and you will be redeemed here, but not with silver.
Thus says the Lord: At first my people went down into Egypt to live there as strangers, and then they were carried off by force to Assyria.

And now, what were they seeking here? Thus says the Lord: My people have been carried off for nothing. Be amazed, and cry out! Thus says the Lord: Because of you my name is always blasphemed among the nations.
Therefore on that day my people shall know my name, for I am the one who speaks: I have come.

Like springtime on the mountains, how beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news of peace, who bring good news of good things! For I will make the voice of your salvation heard when I say to Zion, "Your God shall reign over you."
For the voice of your watchmen has been raised, and they shall rejoice together with that same voice. For you shall see face to face with your own eyes when the Lord has mercy on Zion.
Let the mountains, together with the deserts of Jerusalem, cry out in that joy, for the Lord has had mercy on his people and has delivered Jerusalem.
And the Lord shall reveal his holy arm before all the nations, and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God.
Depart, depart, go out from there, and do not touch what is unclean. Come out from among them and keep yourselves apart, you who carry the vessels of the Lord.
For you shall not go out in confusion or flee like fugitives. The Lord will go before you, and the God of Israel will gather you together.
Behold, my servant shall understand, and he shall be exalted and greatly glorified.
Just as many were astonished at you, so your appearance shall be without glory among men, and your glory without honour among the peoples of men.
So shall many nations marvel at him, and kings shall shut their mouths. For those who had not been told about him shall see, and those who had not heard shall understand.
Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?
We announced this before him as a child, as roots in a waterless land. We saw him, and he had no form and no glory.

But his appearance was without honour, and more diminished than the sons of men. He was a man under blows, and he knows how to bear pains, for he did not turn away his face; they [?], and he was not esteemed.
He bore our weaknesses, and for our pains he comforted us. And we reckoned him to be in pains, and in blows and afflictions.
