But he was wounded for our iniquities, and he was beaten for our sins. The chastening that brought our peace was upon him, and by his wounds we were healed.
All of us had gone astray like sheep: each man went astray in his own way, and the Lord gave him up for our sins.
But he, because of the ill-treatment, does not open his mouth. He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb before the shearer he stood without a sound; so he does not open his mouth.
In his humiliation his judgment was taken away, and who can tell of his generation? For his life is taken from the earth, and for the iniquity of my people he was given up to death.
And I will give the wicked in return for his burial, and the rich in return for his death. For he did no iniquity, and no deceit was found in his mouth.
And the Lord wills to cleanse him of his wound. If you give an offering for their sins, your eyes will see long-lived offspring. And the Lord wills to take away from him the pain of his soul,
to show him light, to form him with understanding, to justify the righteous one, to serve many; and he himself bore their sins.

Therefore he himself will inherit many, and he will divide the spoils of the strong, because his soul was given up to death and he was counted among the lawless. He took upon himself the sins of many, and he was given up for their iniquities.

Rejoice, O barren woman who did not bear; cry out, shout aloud and call, you who were not in labour! For the children of the desolate woman are more than those of the woman who had a husband. And the Lord said:
Enlarge the place of your tent, and set up your courts. Do not hold back: lengthen your cords and strengthen your stakes.
Spread out further to the right and to the left, and your offspring will inherit the nations, and you will settle the desolate cities.

Do not be afraid because you were put to shame, and do not be disgraced because you were reproached. For you will forget the everlasting shame, and you will no longer remember the reproach of your widowhood.
For the Lord who made you, the Lord Almighty is his name, and he who redeemed you, the God of Israel, will himself be called God over all the earth.
The Lord has not called you as a woman who has been forsaken and is faint-hearted, as a woman hated since her youth, said the Lord.
For a moment, a little while, for a single time, I forsook you, and with great mercy I will have mercy on you.
In a little wrath I turned my face away from you, and with everlasting mercy I will have mercy on you, says the Lord, your Redeemer.
Since the flood of Noah this is how it is with me. For I swore to him at that time that I would never again be angry with the earth,

And not even by my word will I remove its mountains, nor will its hills be shaken. In the same way my mercy shall not fail you on my part, nor shall the covenant of your peace be taken away from you, said the Lord. Mercy be upon you.
O humbled one, without rest, until you are comforted! Behold, I will prepare carbuncle for you, and chalcedony as your stone, and I will lay your foundations of sapphire,
and I will build your walls of precious stones, and I will set up your gates with panels of crystal, and I will surround your walls with choice carbuncle.
And all your sons shall be taught by God, and your children shall live in great peace,
and you shall be built up in righteousness. Keep far from falsehood, and you will not be afraid, and terror will not come near you.
Behold, strangers will come to you because of me, and will settle among you, and will flee to you for refuge.
Behold, I have created you, not as a smith who blows on the coals of the fire and brings out a vessel for work. I have created you, and not for destruction and ruin.

No corruptible vessel shall prosper against you, and every voice that rises against you in judgment, you will overcome them all, and those who are guilty shall be in distress. This is the inheritance of the servants of the Lord, and you shall be righteous to me, said the Lord.
You who are thirsty, go to the water, and you who have no silver, come and buy wine and fat without silver and without price.
Why do you buy with silver, when your labour does not satisfy?
Listen to me and eat what is good, and your souls will delight in good things. And I will make an everlasting covenant with you, the holy and faithful [promises] of David.
Behold, I will give him as a witness to the Gentiles, as a ruler and commander to the nations.

Behold, nations that do not know you will call you by name, and peoples that do not know you will make supplication to you, for the sake of your God, the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you.
Seek God, and when you find him, call upon him, and when he draws near to you.
Let the ungodly forsake his ways, and the lawless man his thoughts, and let him return to the Lord, and he will have mercy on him; and our God will forgive our many sins.
For my thoughts are not like your thoughts, nor are my ways like your ways, says the Lord.
But as far as the heavens are from the earth, so far are my ways from your ways, and my thoughts from your thoughts.
For as the rain or the snow comes down from heaven and does not return there until it has watered the earth and made it bring forth and sprout, and gives seed to the sower and bread for food,
so shall my words be that go out from my mouth: they shall not return to me empty until they have accomplished all that I willed, and I will make my ways and my commandments prosper.
For you shall go out with joy and live in gladness. For the mountains and the hills will leap and come to meet you with joy, and all the trees of the field will clap with their branches.
For instead of the bramble the cypress will spring up for you, and instead of the weed [?] the myrtle; and the Lord shall be for a name and an everlasting sign, and it shall not fail.
Thus says the Lord: Keep justice and do righteousness, for my salvation has drawn near to come, and my mercy to be revealed.
Blessed is the man who does this, and the person who accepts this and keeps my sabbaths undefiled, and guards his hands so that he does no falsehood.
Let not the foreigner who has come to the Lord say, "Will the Lord indeed separate me from his people?" And let not the eunuch say, "For I am a dry tree."
For thus says the Lord to the eunuchs who keep my sabbaths, who choose what I desire, and who take hold of my covenants:
I will give them in my house and within my wall a place of renown, better than that of those who have sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name, and it shall not fail.

And the foreigners who come to the Lord to serve him and to love the name of the Lord, so that they may be his menservants and maidservants, and all who keep my sabbath and do not profane it, and who take hold of my covenants,

I will bring them to my holy mountain and make them glad in my house of prayer. Their sacrifices and their offerings shall be acceptable on my altar. For my house shall be called a house of prayer among all the nations.
So said the Lord, who gathered the scattered ones of Israel: for I will gather to them a gathering of all the wild beasts of the field.
Come and eat, all you beasts of the forest.
Now see, they have all been blinded, and they have not known how to understand. They are all cunning dogs that cannot bark. They see visions on their beds, and they love sleep.
The dogs are insatiable in heart and do not know what it is to be full. They are all wicked and do not know understanding. Every one of them follows his own ways, each according to his own mind.
See how the righteous one has perished, and no one takes it to heart. Righteous men are taken away, and no one considers it, for the righteous one has been taken away from the face of falsehood.
And his grave shall be in peace. He has been taken away from the midst.
But you, come here, you lawless sons, offspring of adulterers and of the harlot.
In what were you delighting? Against whom did you open your mouth, and against whom did you stick out your tongue? Are you not children of perdition, a lawless offspring,
who pray to idols under leafy trees, and who slaughtered your children in the ravines, among the rocks, and in places in the valleys?
That is your portion, and this is your inheritance. To them you have offered your offerings, and to them you have brought your sacrifices. Now, shall I not be angered at these things? says the Lord.
On a high and lofty mountain, there is your bed. There you took your sacrifices, toward the back.
And beside the doorposts of your door you set up your memorial. O, if you have turned away from me, what more will harm you [?], for you have loved those who lay with you.
And you multiplied your fornications with them, and you made many who were far from you, and you sent envoys beyond your borders, and you were brought low, even down to Hades.
You grew weary in your many ways, and you did not say, "I will stop," for you grew strong and did this. Therefore you did not entreat me either.

For whom were you anxious, and whom did you fear, that you lied to me and did not remember me, did not consider it in your mind, and did not take me to heart? And I saw you plainly and disregarded you, and you did not fear me.
And I will declare my righteousness and your wickedness, which will do you no good.

When you cry out to them, let them deliver you from your affliction! For the wind has carried all of these away, and the breeze has scattered them. But those who hold fast to me shall be established on the earth and shall inherit my holy mountain,
and they shall say: Clear the ways before him, and remove the stumbling block from the way of my people.

Thus says the Most High, who dwells in the heights forever. His name is Holy among the holy: the Lord, Most High, who rests among the holy ones. He gives patience to the faint-hearted, and gives life to those who are humble in heart.
And I will not take vengeance in anger forever, nor will I always be angry with you. For the spirit shall go forth from me, and I have made all life.
Because of sin I afflicted him a little, and I made him suffer, and I turned my face away from him. And he was grieved and went sorrowfully in his ways.
And I saw his ways and healed him. I gave him courage and gave him true comfort.
Peace upon peace to those who are far off and to those who are near. And the Lord said: I will show them mercy.
But the false ones are like the boiling sea. They shall surge like it and be unable to rest, for their waters are lost in mud and trampled ground.
There is no joy for the ungodly, says the Lord.
Cry out loudly and do not keep silent. Raise your voice like a trumpet, and tell my people their sins, and Jacob his iniquities.

They seek me day after day, and they long to know my ways, as if they were a people that had done righteousness and had not forsaken the judgment of its God. Now they ask me for righteous judgment, and they desire to draw near to God.

And they say: Why is it that we fasted and you did not see, and we humbled our souls and you took no notice? It is because in the days of your fasting your own will is carried out, and you goad all the weak who are under your authority.

Or you fast for lawsuits and quarrels, and you strike your neighbour, the [?], with your fists. So what need have I of such a fast as that, of your coming and crying out before me, as though I would listen to you?

This is not the kind of fast I have chosen, nor the day for a person to humble his soul, by which you have bowed your heads. Even if you now bend your neck like a hoop and spread sackcloth and ashes beneath you, even so it shall not be called a fast or a day acceptable to the Lord.

No, that is not the kind of fast I have chosen, says the Lord. Rather, first of all loosen the knot of your heart and every bond of falsehood, and break up every perverse dealing of oppressive trade. Set the captives free with a release, and tear up every false written bond.
And share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house. If you see someone naked, clothe him, and do not neglect your own kin.
Then your light shall break forth early for you, and your healing shall spring up quickly, and your righteousness shall go before you, and the glory of God shall surround you.

Then you shall cry out, and God will hear you. And even before you ask of him, he will say to you, "Here I am." If you put away from yourself curses, and the stretching out of the hand [?], and the word of murmuring,
and give your bread to the hungry with an open heart, and satisfy the afflicted soul, then your light shall shine forth for you in the darkness, and your darkness shall be like midday.

And your God shall be with you always. You shall be satisfied as your soul desires, and your bones shall be made fat. You shall be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water whose water does not fail.

And your ancient waste places shall be rebuilt, and your foundations shall be everlasting from generation to generation. You shall be called the builder of walls, and there shall be light among your places.

If you turn your foot away from the sabbaths, so as not to do your own will on the holy day, and call the sabbath a delight, holy to God and glorious; if you do not set out your foot to work, and do not speak a word in anger from your mouth,
and you trust in the Lord, then he will lift you up to the good things of the land, and feed you with the portion of Jacob your father. For the mouth of the Lord has spoken this.
Is the hand of the Lord unable to save? Or has his ear grown slow, so that it does not hear?
No, it is your sins that make a separation between God and you, and because of your sins he has turned his face away from you, so as not to have mercy.
For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with sin. Your lips speak lawlessness, and your tongue devises falsehood.
No one speaks justice, and there is no true judgment. They trust in vain things and speak what is empty, for they conceive pain and give birth to vanity.
They have hatched the eggs of asps, and they weave a spider's web. Whoever meant to eat those eggs broke one open and found it addled [?], and in it a viper.
Their web shall not become clothing, nor shall they clothe themselves with their works. For their works are works of lawlessness, and works of falsehood are found in their hands.
Their feet are swift to shed innocent blood, and their thoughts are the thoughts of fools. Destruction and wickedness are in their ways.
They have not known the way of peace. There is no justice in their ways, for the paths they walk are crooked, and they do not know peace.

Therefore justice has gone far from them, and righteousness does not reach them. They waited for light, and it became darkness for them. They looked for the dawn, and they walked in untimely darkness.
They grope for the wall like the blind, and like those blind of eye, so they grope. They stumble at midday as if at midnight.
Like dying bears they gasp for breath, and like stray doves they moan [?]. We waited for justice, and there is no salvation; it has gone far [?] from us.
For our iniquities are many before you, and our sins have risen up against us, and our iniquities are among us. We have recognized our falsehood,
We became ungodly, we lied to the Lord, and we turned away from following our God. We spoke falsehood and became disobedient; we conceived and meditated in our heart false words,
and we turned away from following justice, and we turned our back on judgment, and righteousness withdrew far from us. For truth has failed in their ways, and the straight way could not be travelled.
And truth was taken away from them, and their mind was turned away from understanding. And the Lord saw, and it did not please him, for there was no justice.
He looked, and there was no man; he searched, and there was no helper. And he overcame them with his own arm, and he established his mercy.
And he put on righteousness like a coat of mail, and set his salvation on his head like a helmet, and he put on the garment of vengeance and the adornment of zeal,
with which he will pay back reproach as recompense to his enemies,
and those of the west will fear the name of the Lord, and those of the east his glorious name. For the wrath of the Lord will come forth like a violent river, and it will come with fury.
And the deliverer will come for the sake of Zion, and will turn ungodliness away from Jacob, said the Lord.

And this is my covenant with them, says the Lord: My spirit, which is upon you, and the words that I have put in your mouth, shall not fail from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your offspring, said the Lord, from now and forever.
Be enlightened, be enlightened, O Jerusalem, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord will shine forth upon you.
Behold, darkness will cover the earth, and thick gloom will cover the nations; but the Lord will appear upon you, and his glory will be seen upon you.
And kings will walk in your light, and nations in the brightness of your rising.
Lift up your eyes round about and see all your children gathered together. For all your sons will come from afar, and your daughters will be carried on their shoulders.
Then you will see and rejoice, and you will be afraid and amazed in your heart. For the wealth of the sea and of the nations and of the peoples will be turned toward you, and there will come to you

herds of camels, and the camels of Midian and Ephah will cover you. All will come from Sheba, bringing gold, and they will offer incense to you, and they will proclaim the good news of the salvation of the Lord.
And all the flocks of Kedar will be gathered to you, and the rams of Nebaioth will stand around you, and they will be offered acceptably upon my altar, and my house of prayer will be glorified.
Who are these who fly like clouds, and like doves with their young, toward me? It is Zion.

The islands wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring your children from afar, and their gold and their silver with them, for the sake of the name of the holy Lord and for the Holy One of Israel, so that it may be glorified.
And foreigners will build your walls, and their kings will stand before you to serve you. For in my wrath I struck you, and in my mercy I have loved you.
And your gates will be open continually, day and night, and will not be shut, and they will bring to you the power of the nations, and their kings will be brought to you,
for the nations and kings who do not serve you will perish, and the nations will be utterly laid waste.
And the glory of Lebanon shall come upon you, with the cypress, the pine and the fir. Together my holy place shall be glorified.
And the sons of those who humbled you and of those who provoked you shall come to you in fear, and you shall be called the city of the Lord, Zion of the Holy One of Israel,
because you were forsaken and hated, and there was no one to help you. And you shall become an everlasting joy and a gladness from generation to generation.
And you shall suck the milk of the nations, and you shall eat the wealth of kings, and you shall know that I am the Lord your Saviour, and your Redeemer is the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.

And instead of bronze they shall bring you gold, and instead of iron they shall bring you silver, and instead of wood they shall bring you bronze, and instead of stone, iron. And I will set up your rulers in peace and your overseers in righteousness.
And falsehood shall no longer be heard in your land, nor ruin and misery within your borders. Instead your walls shall be called Salvation, and your gates Carved Work.
And the sun shall not be your light by day, nor shall the rising of the moon give you light at night. Instead God [?] shall be your everlasting light, and the Lord your glory.
For your sun shall not set, and your moon shall not wane. For God himself shall be your everlasting light, and the days of your generation shall be fulfilled.
And your people shall be righteous forever, and they shall inherit the land, and they shall keep the shoot of my planting, the work of my hands, for glorification.
The small one shall become a thousand, and the least a great nation. And I, the Lord, will gather them in due time.

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me; that is why the Lord has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to heal the broken-hearted, to proclaim release to captives and sight to the blind;
to proclaim the favourable year of the Lord and the day of recompense of our God; to comfort all who mourn;

to give to those who mourn for Zion their glory: an anointing of joy instead of ashes for those mourners, and a garment of glory instead of a spirit of despondency. And they shall be called a generation of righteousness and a planting of the Lord for glorification,
and the ancient wastelands shall be rebuilt, and the places laid waste from of old shall be raised up, and the desolate cities, laid waste from generation to generation, shall be renewed.
And the children of strangers shall come to pasture your sheep, and foreigners shall be your ploughmen and vinedressers.
But you shall be called priests of the Lord, and you shall be named servants of your God. You shall eat the strength of the nations, and you shall be admired for their wealth.
Therefore they shall inherit their land a second time, and everlasting joy shall be upon their heads.
For I am the Lord who loves righteousness, and I have hated robbery done through falsehood. I will give the fruit of their labour to the righteous, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.
And their descendants shall be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples. Everyone who sees them shall recognise them, because they are the descendants of men blessed by God.

And they shall rejoice with joy in the Lord. Let my soul rejoice in the Lord, for he has clothed me with the garment of salvation and the adornment of joy. He has set a crown on me like a bridegroom, and adorned me with ornaments like a bride.

And as the earth that makes its flowers grow, and as a garden makes what is sown in it spring up, so shall the Lord make righteousness and gladness shine forth before all the nations. [? stray number "94" in the text, probably a page or verse marker]
For Zion's sake I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until my righteousness goes forth like light, and my salvation blazes forth like lightning.
And the nations shall see my righteousness, and kings my glory. And you shall be called by your new name, which the Lord himself shall name.
And you shall be a crown of beauty in the hand of the Lord, and a royal diadem in the hand of your God.
And you shall no longer be called Forsaken, and your land shall no longer be called Desolate; but you shall be called by my name, and your land shall be called Inhabited World.
And as a young man settles down with a virgin, so shall your sons settle in you. And as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so shall the Lord rejoice over you.
And on your walls, Jerusalem, I have set watchmen all day and all night, who shall never be silent in remembering the Lord.
For there is no one like you, if you are guided aright. And Jerusalem shall be a joy upon the earth.

The Lord has sworn by his glory and by the might of his arm: "I will no longer give your wheat and your food to your enemies, and the sons of foreigners shall no longer drink your wine, for which you laboured.
But those who gather it in shall eat it and praise the Lord, and those who gathered it shall drink it in my holy courts."
Go out through my gates, and make a way for my people; throw the stones out of the roads, and raise a signal to the nations.
For behold, the Lord has made it heard to the end of the earth. Say to the daughter of Zion: "Behold, your Saviour is coming, and his reward is with him, and his works go before him."
And he shall call it a holy people, redeemed by the Lord; and you shall be called a City Sought Out, and not Forsaken.
Who is this who comes from Edom, with the crimson of his garments from Bozrah? He is splendid in his apparel, and fierce with great strength. "I speak righteousness and the judgment of salvation."
"Why is your apparel crimson, and your garments like those of the treaders of a winepress,
full of what has been trodden?" "And of the nations there was no man with me. I trampled them in my wrath, and crushed them in my anger, and poured out their blood on the ground,
for the day of retribution has come upon them, and the year of redemption has arrived.
And I looked, and there was no helper; and I watched, and there was no one to give support; so my own arm delivered me, and my wrath came on.
And I trampled them in my anger, and made them drunk with my wrath, and poured out their blood on the ground."

For I have remembered the mercy of the Lord, the virtuous deeds of the Lord in all that he has rendered to us. The Lord is a good judge over the house of Israel. May he send upon us according to his mercy . . . [?]
And he said: "Is this people of mine not my children? And they will not despise me." And he became their Saviour

from all their affliction, for it was no messenger, nor an angel, but the Lord himself who saved them, because he loved them, and he protected them. He himself saved them, and he lifted them up and exalted them all the days of old.
But they rebelled and angered his Holy Spirit, and he turned against them as an enemy. The Lord himself fought against them.
Then he remembered the days of old. Where is the one who brought up the shepherd of the sheep, and where is the one who put the Holy Spirit upon them?
He led Moses by his right hand. With the arm of his glory he made the waters strong before him, to make himself an everlasting name.
He led them out of the deep like a horse through the wilderness, and they did not grow weary,
and like a single [?] on the plain. The Spirit came from the Lord and guided them. In this way you led your people and made yourself a glorious name.
Turn back from heaven, O Lord, and look down from the holy temple of your glory. Where is your great mercy and your compassion, from the time when you bore with us, O Lord?
For you are our Father. Abraham did not know us, but you are our Father. Save us, for your name has been upon us from the beginning.
Why, O Lord, have you made us stray from your way and hardened our hearts, so that we do not fear you? Turn back for the sake of your servants and for the sake of the tribes of your inheritance,
so that we too may inherit a small part of your holy mountain.
We have become as we were at the beginning, when you did not rule over us and your name was not called upon us.
If you open the heavens, the mountains will be seized with trembling before you; they will melt
as wax melts in the fire. Fire will burn up your enemies, and your name will be made known to those who hate you. The nations will tremble before your face
when you do glorious deeds; the mountains will be seized with trembling before you.
Since ages past we have not heard of any God but you, and our eyes have not seen one. Your works are true, the mercy that you have shown to those who wait patiently for you.
For mercy will come to meet those who do what is right, and they will remember your ways. Look, you were angry, and we sinned against you, and so we went astray,
and all of us became unclean; all our righteousness is like the rags of a menstruating woman. All of us fell like leaves because of our lawlessness, and so the wind carried us away.
There is no one who calls upon your name or remembers to cling to you, for you have turned your face away from us and handed us over because of our sins.
And now, O Lord, you are our Father, and we are all like clay, the work of your hands.
Do not be utterly angry with us, O Lord, and do not remember our sins at this time. Now look upon us, for all of us are your people,
and your holy city, Zion, has become desolate, and Jerusalem has become like a wilderness.
The temple of our holiness has become a curse. The glory that our fathers blessed has been burned with fire, and everything we held glorious has been brought to ruin.
And through all this you have held back, O Lord, and have humbled us greatly.
I was made manifest to those who did not ask for me, and I was found by those who did not seek me. I said, "Here I am," to the nation that did not call on my name.
I stretched out my hands all day long to a disobedient and contentious people, who walk in a way that is not good, but follow after their sins.
This is the people that provoked me to anger before my face continually. They sacrifice in their gardens and burn incense to demons on their bricks.
They dwell in tombs and in caves, and they lie down to sleep [?] for the sake of dreams. They eat the flesh of swine and drink the broth of their sacrifices, and all their vessels are defiled.
They say, "Keep away from me; do not come near me, for I am holy." This is the smoke of my wrath; a fire burns upon it all the days.
Behold, it is written before me, and I will not keep silent until I repay into their bosom

all their sins, those of all their days and those of their fathers together, says the Lord. They burned incense on the mountains and reproached me on the hills, and I will repay their deeds first into their bosom.

Thus says the Lord: When a grape is found in a cluster, people say, "Do not destroy it, for the blessing of the Lord is in it." So will I do for the sake of the one who serves me. For this reason I will not destroy them all,
and I will bring forth seed from Jacob and from Judah, and it shall inherit my holy mountain. My chosen ones and my servants shall inherit it, and they shall dwell there.
In the thickets there shall be folds for flocks, and the valley of Achor shall be a resting place for the herds of my people who sought me.
But you have forsaken me and forgotten my holy mountain. You prepared a table for Fortune and filled a mixing bowl for the demon.

Now I will hand you over to the sword, and all of you shall fall in the slaughter. For I called you and you did not obey me; I spoke to you and you did not listen to me. You did evil before me and chose what I did not want.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, those who serve me shall eat, but you shall be hungry; those who serve me shall drink, but you shall be thirsty.
Those who serve me shall rejoice with gladness of heart, but you shall cry out from the pain of your heart, and you shall cry out from the anguish of your spirit.
For you shall leave your name to my chosen ones as a thing to be sated with, and the Lord shall destroy you. But those who serve me shall be called by a new name.

Whoever is blessed on the earth shall bless the true God, and those who swear on the earth shall swear by the true God. For the former affliction shall be forgotten, and it shall no longer come into their heart.
For there shall be a new heaven and a new earth. They shall no longer remember the former things, and these shall not come into their heart,
but they shall find joy and gladness in whatever I create. For behold, I will make Jerusalem a joy and my people a gladness.
I will rejoice over Jerusalem and be glad over my people. The sound of weeping and the sound of crying shall no longer be heard in it.

And there shall no longer be anyone there born untimely and incomplete, nor an old man who has not filled out his days. For the child shall die a hundred years old, and the old man shall die as a youth, and the youth who dies before he is a hundred years old shall be accursed.
And they shall build houses and live in them themselves. And they shall plant vineyards and eat their fruit themselves.

And they shall no longer build so that others may live there, nor shall they plant so that others may eat. For the days of my people shall be like the days of the tree of life, and they shall wear out the works of their labours.
But my chosen ones shall not toil in vain, nor shall they bear children for a curse, for they are a race blessed by God.
And before they cry out, I will hear them, and before they speak, I will say to them: "Here I am."

At that time wolves and lambs shall graze together, and the lion shall eat straw like the ox, and the serpent shall eat earth as its bread. And they shall not harm anyone or do damage on my holy mountain, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool for my feet. What kind of house will you build for me, said the Lord, or what place could be my resting place?
For my hand made all these things, and all these things are mine, said the Lord. And to whom shall I look, except to the one who is humble and quiet, and who trembles at my words?

But the lawless person who offers me a calf as a sacrifice is to me like someone who strikes a man. And whoever offers a sheep shall be like someone who kills a dog. And whoever brings a grain offering shall be like someone who pours out pig's blood. And whoever burns incense as a memorial offering shall be like a blasphemer. For they have chosen their own ways and their abominations, and their soul has desired them.
And I will choose their mockeries [?] and repay them for their sin, for I called them and they did not listen to me. They did evil in my sight and chose what I do not want.

Now hear the word of the Lord, you who tremble at his words. Call "brothers" those who hate you and those who despise you, so that the name of the Lord may be glorified and be revealed with joy in Jerusalem. You shall rejoice, and they shall be put to shame.
A voice of crying from the city, and a voice from the temple: the voice of the Lord who repays. He will repay his enemies what they deserve.
Before the pregnant woman had given birth, and before the pains of childbirth had come upon her, she was delivered and bore a male child.
Who has heard, or who has seen, such a wonder: that the earth conceived in a single day, and gave birth to a whole nation at once? For Zion conceived and gave birth to her children.
But I gave such a hope, and you did not remember me, said the Lord. Did I not create both the one who gives birth and the barren woman?
Rejoice together, Jerusalem, and gather in her, all you who love her. Rejoice with her with joy, all you who mourned for her,
so that you may nurse and be satisfied at the breasts of her consolation, and so that you may delight to the full in the coming in of her glory.

For thus says the Lord: Behold, I will turn peace toward them like a river, and like a torrent it shall bring the glory of the nations. Their children shall be carried on the shoulders and comforted upon their knees.
As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you, and you shall be comforted in Jerusalem.
And you shall see, and your hearts shall rejoice, and your bones shall sprout like green herbs. The hand of the Lord shall be revealed to those who fear him, and he shall threaten the disobedient.
For behold, the Lord shall come like fire, and his chariots like a fierce whirlwind, to repay his vengeance in wrath and his rebuke with a flame of fire.
For by the fire of the Lord all the earth shall be judged, and all flesh by his sword; for many shall be wounded by the Lord.
But those who justify themselves and purify themselves in the gardens, and eat swine's flesh before the gates, and those abominations and the mouse, shall be destroyed together, says the Lord.
For because of their deeds and their thoughts I am coming to gather all nations and tongues. They shall come and see my glory.

And I will leave a sign among them, and I will send those of them who are saved to the nations: to Tarshish, and Put, and Lud, and Meshech, and Tubal, and to Greece, and to the distant islands, which have not heard my name nor seen my glory; and they shall declare my glory among the nations.

And they shall bring your brothers from all the nations as an offering to the Lord, with horses and chariots, with tents and mules and with sunshades, to the holy city of Jerusalem, said the Lord, just as the children of Israel offered their sacrifices to me with singing in the temple of the Lord.
And from among them I will take some as priests and Levites, says the Lord.
For just as the new heaven and the new earth that I make shall remain before me, says the Lord, so shall your offspring and your name remain.
And it shall be from new moon to new moon, and from sabbath to sabbath, that all flesh shall come to worship before me in Jerusalem, said the Lord.

And they shall go out and see the bones of the men who transgressed against me; for their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched, and they shall be a spectacle to all flesh . . . [?]
